This page documents the parallelization capabilities in CPPTRAJ, which includes support for shared-memory (OpenMP), distributed-memory (MPI), and GPU acceleration (CUDA/HIP). Understanding these parallelization options is essential for efficient processing of large trajectory datasets and complex analyses.

For information on executing commands in parallel, see [Parallel Analysis](#3.1) and for performance tuning see [Optimization](#6.2).

## Overview of Parallelization Methods

CPPTRAJ supports three main types of parallelization that can be used independently or in combination:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Parallelization Methods"
        OpenMP["OpenMP Parallelization"]
        MPI["MPI Parallelization"]
        GPU["GPU Acceleration"]
    end
    
    subgraph "OpenMP Features"
        OpenMP --> ThreadParallel["Thread-Level Parallelism"]
        ThreadParallel --> SharedMemory["Shared Memory Model"]
        ThreadParallel --> FrameDecomp["Frame Decomposition"]
        ThreadParallel --> TaskParallel["Task Parallelism"]
    end
    
    subgraph "MPI Features"
        MPI --> DistParallel["Distributed Parallelism"]
        DistParallel --> NormalMode["Normal Mode"]
        DistParallel --> EnsembleMode["Ensemble Mode"]
        DistParallel --> DataSync["Data Synchronization"]
    end
    
    subgraph "GPU Features"
        GPU --> CUDASupport["CUDA Support"]
        GPU --> HIPSupport["HIP/ROCm Support"]
        GPU --> AcceleratedActions["Accelerated Actions"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/Cpptraj.cpp:29-61](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/configure:2-109](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/Parallel.cpp](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj)

## Building with Parallelization Support

Each parallelization method requires specific compiler flags and libraries to be enabled during the build process.

### OpenMP Support

OpenMP parallelization is enabled with the `-openmp` flag during configuration:

```bash
./configure -openmp [compiler]
```

This sets up compiler flags for OpenMP support, allowing thread-level parallelism for actions and analyses that support it.

### MPI Support

MPI parallelization is enabled with the `-mpi` flag (for standard MPI implementations) or `-intelmpi` (for Intel MPI):

```bash
./configure -mpi [compiler]
```

### GPU Support

CUDA or HIP support for NVIDIA or AMD GPUs respectively can be enabled with:

```bash
./configure -cuda [compiler]   # For NVIDIA GPUs
./configure -hip [compiler]    # For AMD GPUs
```

The CUDA compute capability can be specified via the `SHADER_MODEL` environment variable.

Sources: [src/configure:11-109](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/configure:177-196](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj)

## Parallelization Architecture

The following diagram illustrates how the different parallelization methods interact within CPPTRAJ:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Cpptraj["Cpptraj"]
    CpptrajState["CpptrajState"]
    
    subgraph "Processing Modes"
        NormalMode["Normal Mode"]
        EnsembleMode["Ensemble Mode"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parallel Processing"
        MPIComm["MPI Communication Layer"]
        OMP["OpenMP Threading"]
        CUDAKernels["CUDA/HIP Kernels"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Action Processing"
        ActionList["ActionList"]
        ParallelActions["Parallel Actions"]
        SequentialActions["Sequential Actions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis Processing"
        AnalysisList["AnalysisList"]
        ParallelAnalyses["Parallel Analyses"]
        SequentialAnalyses["Sequential Analyses"]
    end
    
    Cpptraj --> CpptrajState
    CpptrajState --> NormalMode
    CpptrajState --> EnsembleMode
    
    NormalMode --> MPIComm
    EnsembleMode --> MPIComm
    
    MPIComm --> ActionList
    MPIComm --> AnalysisList
    
    ActionList --> ParallelActions
    ActionList --> SequentialActions
    AnalysisList --> ParallelAnalyses
    AnalysisList --> SequentialAnalyses
    
    ParallelActions --> OMP
    ParallelActions --> CUDAKernels
    ParallelAnalyses --> OMP
    ParallelAnalyses --> CUDAKernels
```

Sources: [src/Cpptraj.cpp:29-61](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/Parallel.cpp](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/ActionList.cpp:78-112](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/AnalysisList.cpp:42-95](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj)

## OpenMP Parallelization

OpenMP is used for shared-memory parallelism, primarily within individual actions and analyses. When enabled, CPPTRAJ automatically detects and uses available threads:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "OpenMP Parallelization Model"
        ActionFrame["Action Frame Processing"]
        DataCalc["Data Calculations"]
        
        ActionFrame --> |"#pragma omp parallel"| Frame1["Frame Chunk 1"]
        ActionFrame --> |"#pragma omp parallel"| Frame2["Frame Chunk 2"]
        ActionFrame --> |"#pragma omp parallel"| FrameN["Frame Chunk N"]
        
        DataCalc --> |"#pragma omp parallel"| Calc1["Calculation 1"]
        DataCalc --> |"#pragma omp parallel"| Calc2["Calculation 2"]
        DataCalc --> |"#pragma omp parallel"| CalcN["Calculation N"]
    end
```

Several computationally intensive operations benefit from OpenMP parallelization:

| Feature | Parallelization Method | Performance Impact |
|---------|------------------------|-------------------|
| Frame processing | Frame-level parallelism | High for multiple frames |
| Distance calculations | Loop-level parallelism | High for large systems |
| RMSD calculations | Task-level parallelism | Medium to high |
| Grid-based calculations | Domain decomposition | High for large grids |
| Clustering | Work distribution | Variable by algorithm |

The number of OpenMP threads can be controlled using the standard `OMP_NUM_THREADS` environment variable before running CPPTRAJ.

Sources: [src/Cpptraj.cpp:113-114](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/ActionList.cpp:78-112](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj)

## MPI Parallelization

CPPTRAJ implements two main modes of MPI parallelization:

1. **Normal Mode**: Distributes frames of a single trajectory across multiple processes
2. **Ensemble Mode**: Each process handles a different trajectory from an ensemble

### MPI Communication Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "MPI Communication Layers"
        direction TB
        WorldComm["World Communicator (All Processes)"]
        TrajComm["Trajectory Communicator (Data Frame Distribution)"]
        EnsembleComm["Ensemble Communicator (Ensemble Distribution)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Normal Mode"
        direction LR
        Master["Master Process"] --> Worker1["Worker 1"]
        Master --> Worker2["Worker 2"]
        Master --> WorkerN["Worker N"]
        
        subgraph "Data Flow"
            direction TB
            TrajRead["Trajectory Read"]
            FrameDistribution["Frame Distribution"]
            ActionExecution["Action Execution"]
            ResultCollection["Result Collection"]
            DataSynchronization["Data Synchronization"]
        end
    end
    
    subgraph "Ensemble Mode"
        direction TB
        Ensemble1["Ensemble Member 1"] 
        Ensemble2["Ensemble Member 2"]
        EnsembleN["Ensemble Member N"]
        
        subgraph "Independent Processing"
            direction TB
            IndividualTraj["Individual Trajectory"]
            LocalActions["Local Action Processing"]
            GlobalSync["Global Synchronization"]
        end
    end
    
    WorldComm --> TrajComm
    WorldComm --> EnsembleComm
    
    TrajComm --> Master
    EnsembleComm --> Ensemble1
    EnsembleComm --> Ensemble2
    EnsembleComm --> EnsembleN
```

Sources: [src/CpptrajState.cpp:67-125](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/CpptrajState.cpp:632-765](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj)

### MPI Process Flow

The process flow differs significantly between Normal and Ensemble modes:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Master as Master Process
    participant Workers as Worker Processes
    participant DSL as DataSetList
    
    Note over Master,Workers: Normal Mode
    Master->>Workers: Broadcast topology
    Master->>Workers: Distribute frame ranges
    loop Each frame range
        Workers->>Workers: Process actions
        Workers->>Workers: Generate local data
    end
    Workers->>Master: Gather results
    Master->>DSL: Synchronize datasets
    
    Note over Master,Workers: Ensemble Mode
    Master->>Workers: Assign ensemble members
    loop Each ensemble independently
        Workers->>Workers: Process complete trajectories
        Workers->>Workers: Generate local data
    end
    Workers->>Master: Synchronize for analysis
    Master->>DSL: Combine ensemble results
```

### Parallel Analysis Considerations

Not all analyses can be parallelized with MPI. The `AnalysisList` class checks if an analysis supports parallelization and adapts accordingly:

```cpp
// For parallel-capable analyses:
if (ana->ptr_->IsParallel()) {
  ret = ana->ptr_->Analyze();
} else {
  // For non-parallel analyses, only run on master:
  if (Parallel::TrajComm().Master())
    ret = ana->ptr_->Analyze();
  else
    ret = Analysis::OK;
  // Broadcast result to other processes
  Parallel::World().MasterBcast(&ret, 1, MPI_INT);
}
```

Data synchronization between processes occurs after action processing to ensure all analyses have access to complete datasets.

Sources: [src/AnalysisList.cpp:42-95](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/CpptrajState.cpp:632-765](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj)

## GPU Acceleration

CPPTRAJ supports GPU acceleration through CUDA (for NVIDIA GPUs) and HIP (for AMD GPUs).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "CPU Processing"
        CPUActions["CPU Action Execution"]
        DataPrep["Data Preparation"]
        ResultProcessing["Result Processing"]
    end
    
    subgraph "GPU Acceleration"
        GPUKernels["GPU Kernels"]
        CUDASupport["CUDA Implementation"]
        HIPSupport["HIP Implementation"]
        
        GPUKernels --> CUDASupport
        GPUKernels --> HIPSupport
    end
    
    DataPrep --> |"Memory Transfer"| GPUKernels
    GPUKernels --> |"Memory Transfer"| ResultProcessing
    
    CPUActions --- |"Non-accelerated portions"| ResultProcessing
```

GPU-accelerated functionality includes:

1. GIST (Grid Inhomogeneous Solvation Theory) calculations
2. Certain distance-based calculations
3. Closest water calculations

The system automatically detects GPU devices at startup and reports their capabilities:

```
| CUDA device: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080
| Available GPU memory: 10,240,000,000 bytes
| Compute capability: 8.6
```

For actions that support GPU acceleration, the calculation-intensive portions are offloaded to the GPU, while the CPU handles data preparation and post-processing of results.

Sources: [src/Cpptraj.cpp:120-141](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/Action_Closest.cpp](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/Action_GIST.cpp](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj)

## Performance Considerations

### Selecting the Right Parallelization Method

| Scenario | Recommended Parallelization |
|----------|----------------------------|
| Single large trajectory | MPI Normal mode + OpenMP |
| Multiple trajectories/replicates | MPI Ensemble mode |
| Compute-intensive analyses | OpenMP + GPU if supported |
| Limited memory systems | MPI to distribute memory usage |
| Interactive usage | OpenMP only (MPI doesn't support interactive mode) |

### Practical Guidelines

1. **OpenMP Scaling**: Performance generally scales well to the number of physical cores, but hyperthreading benefits vary by action.

2. **MPI Process Count**: For Normal mode, use a process count that divides the trajectory frame count evenly to avoid load imbalance.

3. **Hybrid Parallelization**: When using both MPI and OpenMP, adjust `OMP_NUM_THREADS` to ensure you don't oversubscribe CPU cores.

4. **GPU Memory Management**: For very large systems, monitor GPU memory usage as some actions may require significant GPU memory.

5. **I/O Bottlenecks**: When processing many frames with multiple MPI processes, I/O can become a bottleneck. Consider using SSD storage or high-performance parallel filesystems.

Sources: [src/Cpptraj.cpp:5-141](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj), [src/CpptrajState.cpp:632-765](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj)

This document describes the fundamental data structures that CPPTRAJ uses to represent molecular systems and analysis data. These structures form the foundation for all trajectory processing, analysis, and data management operations within the software. For information about the overall system architecture, see [Overview](#1).

## Molecular Representation

CPPTRAJ uses several core classes to represent molecular systems, with `Topology` as the central container that holds information about atoms, residues, molecules, and their connectivity.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Topology {
        +std::vector<Atom> atoms_
        +std::vector<Residue> residues_
        +std::vector<Molecule> molecules_
        +Box parmBox_
        +BondArray bonds_
        +BondArray bondsh_
        +AngleArray angles_
        +DihedralArray dihedrals_
        +NonbondParmType nonbond_
        +int Natom()
        +int Nres()
        +int Nmol()
        +DetermineMolecules()
        +SetupIntegerMask(AtomMask&)
    }
    
    class Atom {
        +NameType name_
        +double mass_
        +double charge_
        +AtomicElementType element_
        +int resNum_
        +int atomNum_
        +std::vector<int> bondArray_
        +DetermineElement()
        +AddBondToIdx(int)
    }
    
    class Residue {
        +NameType name_
        +int firstAtom_
        +int lastAtom_
        +int originalResNum_
        +char icode_
        +std::string chainID_
        +bool terminal_
        +NameName()
        +NameIsSolvent()
    }
    
    class Molecule {
        +Unit molUnit_
        +bool isSolvent_
        +NumAtoms()
        +MolUnit()
        +SetSolvent()
    }
    
    Topology *-- "many" Atom : contains
    Topology *-- "many" Residue : contains
    Topology *-- "many" Molecule : contains
    Topology *-- "many" BondType : contains
    Topology *-- "many" AngleType : contains
    Topology *-- "many" DihedralType : contains
    Atom -- Residue : belongs to
    Residue -- Molecule : part of
```

The `Topology` class is the central container that holds all information about the molecular system structure. It manages collections of atoms, residues, molecules, and their connectivity through bonds, angles, and dihedrals.

Sources: [src/Topology.h:16-255](), [src/Topology.cpp:15-183]()

### Atom

The `Atom` class represents individual atoms and stores properties such as name, mass, charge, and element type. It also maintains bonding information through a list of indices to atoms it is bonded to.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Atom {
        +NameType name_
        +double mass_
        +double charge_
        +AtomicElementType element_
        +int resNum_
        +int molNum_
        +std::vector<int> bondArray_
        +Name()
        +SetName()
        +Mass()
        +SetMass()
        +Charge()
        +SetCharge()
        +Element()
        +DetermineElement()
        +AddBondToIdx(int)
        +RemoveBondToIdx(int)
    }
    
    class AtomicElementType {
        <<enumeration>>
        UNKNOWN_ELEMENT
        HYDROGEN
        CARBON
        NITROGEN
        OXYGEN
        etc...
    }
    
    Atom -- AtomicElementType : has
```

Sources: [src/Atom.h:6-89](), [src/Atom.cpp:6-22]()

### Residue and Molecule

Residues are groups of atoms that form functional units (like amino acids or nucleotides), while molecules are collections of atoms connected by bonds.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Residue {
        +NameType name_
        +int firstAtom_
        +int lastAtom_
        +int originalResNum_
        +char icode_
        +std::string chainID_
        +bool terminal_
        +FirstAtom()
        +LastAtom()
        +SetFirstAtom()
        +SetLastAtom()
        +NameIsSolvent()
    }
    
    class Molecule {
        +Unit molUnit_
        +bool isSolvent_
        +NumAtoms()
        +MolUnit()
        +SetSolvent()
        +IsSolvent()
    }
    
    class Unit {
        +SegIdxArray segidx_
        +nSegments()
        +Front()
        +Back()
    }
    
    Molecule *-- Unit : contains
    Unit -- Residue : references
```

Molecules track their constituent atoms through the `Unit` class, which maintains segments of contiguous atom indices.

Sources: [src/Topology.h:90-105](), [src/Topology.cpp:90-176]()

### Connectivity: Bonds, Angles, and Dihedrals

Molecular connectivity is represented by classes for bonds, angles, and dihedrals, along with their associated parameters.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class BondType {
        +int a1_
        +int a2_
        +int idx_
        +A1()
        +A2()
        +SetIdx()
    }
    
    class AngleType {
        +int a1_
        +int a2_
        +int a3_
        +int idx_
        +A1()
        +A2()
        +A3()
    }
    
    class DihedralType {
        +int a1_
        +int a2_
        +int a3_
        +int a4_
        +int idx_
        +A1()
        +A2()
        +A3()
        +A4()
    }
    
    class BondParmType {
        +double rk_
        +double req_
        +Rk()
        +Req()
    }
    
    class AngleParmType {
        +double tk_
        +double teq_
        +Tk()
        +Teq()
    }
    
    class DihedralParmType {
        +double pk_
        +double pn_
        +double phase_
        +double scee_
        +double scnb_
        +Pk()
        +Pn()
        +Phase()
    }
    
    BondType -- BondParmType : references
    AngleType -- AngleParmType : references
    DihedralType -- DihedralParmType : references
```

Sources: [src/ParameterTypes.h:22-45](), [src/Topology.h:111-147]()

## Coordinate Management

### Frame

The `Frame` class is a fundamental data structure that stores the coordinates, velocities, and forces for all atoms in a molecular system at a single point in time.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Frame {
        +double* X_
        +double* V_
        +double* F_
        +std::vector<double> Mass_
        +Box box_
        +double T_
        +double pH_
        +double time_
        +int natom_
        +int ncoord_
        +int step_
        +SetupFrame(int)
        +AddXYZ(double*)
        +SetCoordinates(Frame, AtomMask)
        +RMSD(Frame, bool)
        +MaskCenter(AtomMask)
        +Translate(Vec3)
        +Rotate(Matrix33)
    }
    
    class Box {
        +double boxX_
        +double boxY_
        +double boxZ_
        +double alpha_
        +double beta_
        +double gamma_
        +CellShape type_
        +HasBox()
        +SetBox(double, double, double)
        +SetTruncOct()
        +SetNoBox()
    }
    
    class CoordinateInfo {
        +Box box_
        +bool hasVel_
        +bool hasForce_
        +bool hasTemp_
        +bool hasTime_
        +HasVel()
        +HasForce()
        +TrajBox()
    }
    
    Frame *-- Box : contains
    Frame -- CoordinateInfo : describes
```

The `Frame` class is designed to efficiently store and manipulate atomic coordinates (X_), velocities (V_), and forces (F_). It supports various operations like RMSD calculations, translations, and rotations.

Sources: [src/Frame.h:9-193](), [src/Frame.cpp:9-117]()

### AtomMask

`AtomMask` provides a way to select specific atoms from a topology using mask expressions.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class AtomMask {
        +std::vector<int> Selected_
        +int Natom_
        +char maskChar_
        +std::string maskString_
        +Nselected()
        +AddSelectedAtom(int)
        +AddAtomRange(int, int)
        +SetupMask(Topology)
        +MaskString()
        +SetMaskString(string)
        +ResetMask()
        +InvertMask()
    }
    
    class MaskToken {
        +std::string Token
        +std::vector<std::string> tokens_
        +Type tokenType_
        +ParseMask(std::string)
        +MaskTokens()
    }
    
    AtomMask --|> MaskToken : inherits
```

`AtomMask` is used throughout CPPTRAJ to select subsets of atoms for various operations. It can be created from mask expressions like `:1-10@CA,C,N` (selecting backbone atoms from residues 1-10).

Sources: [src/AtomMask.h:6-104](), [src/AtomMask.cpp:6-54]()

## Data Management

CPPTRAJ uses a sophisticated data management system centered around the `DataSet` hierarchy to store and process analysis results.

### DataSet Hierarchy

`DataSet` is the base class for all types of data that can be collected during analysis. Specific types inherit from this base class.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DataSet {
        <<abstract>>
        +MetaData meta_
        +TextFormat format_
        +std::vector<Dimension> dim_
        +DataType dType_
        +DataGroup dGroup_
        +virtual Size()
        +virtual Info()
        +virtual WriteBuffer()
        +virtual Allocate()
        +virtual Add()
        +virtual Append()
    }
    
    class DataSet_1D {
        <<abstract>>
        +Xcrd(int)
        +Dcrd(int)
        +Dval(int)
        +SetDval(int, double)
        +AssignWithLabels(DataSet_1D)
    }
    
    class DataSet_double {
        +std::vector<double> Data_
        +Add(size_t, void*)
        +operator[](int)
        +Append(DataSet*)
    }
    
    class DataSet_Vector {
        +std::vector<Vec3> Data_
        +Add(size_t, void*)
        +Append(DataSet*)
    }
    
    class DataSet_Matrix_3D {
        +MatrixType matrix_
        +MatrixIdx()
        +SetElement()
        +GetElement()
    }
    
    class DataSet_Coords {
        <<abstract>>
        +LoadFrame(int, Frame&)
        +CoordsSetup(Topology)
        +Top()
    }
    
    DataSet <|-- DataSet_1D : inherits
    DataSet <|-- DataSet_Matrix_3D : inherits
    DataSet <|-- DataSet_Coords : inherits
    DataSet_1D <|-- DataSet_double : inherits
    DataSet_1D <|-- DataSet_Vector : inherits
```

The `DataSet` hierarchy supports many data types, from simple 1D arrays to complex structures like coordinate sets and matrices.

Sources: [src/DataSet.h:13-166](), [src/DataSet.cpp:5-37]()

### DataSetList

`DataSetList` manages collections of DataSet objects, providing functions for adding, finding, and accessing datasets.

```mermaid
classDiagram

        +AddSet(DataSet::DataType, MetaData)
        +AddSetAsCopy(DataSet*)

        +RemoveSet(DataSet*)

        +ClearAll()
    }
    
    DataSetList o-- "many" DataSet : manages
```

Sources: [src/DataSetList.h:22-103](), [src/DataSetList.cpp:43-126]()

### DataFile and DataFileList

The `DataFile` class handles writing data to files in various formats, while `DataFileList` manages multiple output files.

```mermaid
classDiagram

        +virtual processWriteArgs(ArgList)

    DataFileList o-- "many" DataFile : manages
    DataFile *-- DataIO : uses
    DataFile o-- "many" DataSet : contains
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.h:8-111](), [src/DataFile.cpp:38-142](), [src/DataFileList.h:9-39](), [src/DataFileList.cpp:10-43]()

## Memory Management and Performance Considerations

CPPTRAJ's core data structures are designed with performance in mind, particularly for large molecular systems and trajectory analysis.

### Frame Memory Layout

The `Frame` class uses contiguous arrays for coordinates, velocities, and forces to maximize cache efficiency and enable vectorized operations:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Frame
        X["X_[natom*3]"]
        V["V_[natom*3] (optional)"]
        F["F_[natom*3] (optional)"]
        Mass["Mass_[natom]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Memory Layout"
        XLayout["x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 ... xN yN zN"]
        VLayout["vx1 vy1 vz1 ... vxN vyN vzN"]
        FLayout["fx1 fy1 fz1 ... fxN fyN fzN"]
    end
    
    X --> XLayout
    V --> VLayout
    F --> FLayout
```

Sources: [src/Frame.h:33-103](), [src/Frame.cpp:371-407]()

### Data Sets and Disk Caching

For memory-intensive analyses, CPPTRAJ provides options for disk caching of large datasets:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    DataSetList --> |"useDiskCache_=true"| DiskCache["Disk-Cached Sets"]
    DataSetList --> |"useDiskCache_=false"| MemorySets["Memory-Resident Sets"]
    
    DiskCache --> |"Integer"| DataSet_integer_disk
    DiskCache --> |"Matrices"| DataSet_MatrixDbl
    
    MemorySets --> DataSet_integer_mem
    MemorySets --> OtherSets["Other Memory Sets"]
```

Sources: [src/DataSetList.cpp:40-108]()

This summarizes the core data structures in CPPTRAJ and their relationships. These structures form the foundation for all molecular system representation, coordinate manipulation, and data analysis capabilities within the software.

# Page: Topology

# Topology

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/Atom.cpp](src/Atom.cpp)
- [src/Atom.h](src/Atom.h)
- [src/ParameterTypes.h](src/ParameterTypes.h)
- [src/Parm_Amber.cpp](src/Parm_Amber.cpp)
- [src/Parm_Amber.h](src/Parm_Amber.h)
- [src/Topology.cpp](src/Topology.cpp)
- [src/Topology.h](src/Topology.h)

</details>



The Topology class represents the complete molecular structure and parameters of a chemical system in CPPTRAJ. It serves as a comprehensive container for atoms, residues, molecules, and the connections between them (bonds, angles, dihedrals), as well as force field parameters. This page documents the internal structure and functionality of the Topology class, which is a fundamental data structure in CPPTRAJ's architecture.

For information about how topologies are read from files, see the Trajectory Processing Pipeline section [3.2](#3.2).

## Class Overview

The Topology class encapsulates all structural information about a molecular system. It contains collections of atoms, residues, and molecules, along with their connectivity information and force field parameters. The class serves as the backbone for most operations in CPPTRAJ that require knowledge of molecular structure.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Topology {
        -std::vector~Atom~ atoms_
        -std::vector~Residue~ residues_
        -std::vector~Molecule~ molecules_
        -BondArray bonds_
        -BondArray bondsh_
        -AngleArray angles_
        -AngleArray anglesh_
        -DihedralArray dihedrals_
        -DihedralArray dihedralsh_
        -NonbondParmType nonbond_
        -Box parmBox_
        +Natom() int
        +Nres() int
        +Nmol() int
        +DetermineMolecules() int
        +AddBond(int, int, int)
        +AddAngle(int, int, int, int)
        +AddDihedral(DihedralType, int)
        +SetupIntegerMask(AtomMask&) int
    }

    class Atom {
        -double charge_
        -double mass_
        -NameType aname_
        -NameType atype_
        -AtomicElementType element_
        -int resnum_
        -int mol_
        -std::vector~int~ bonds_
        +Name() NameType
        +Charge() double
        +Mass() double
        +Element() AtomicElementType
        +AddBondToIdx(int)
    }

    class Residue {
        -NameType name_
        -int firstAtom_
        -int lastAtom_
        -int originalResNum_
        -char icode_
        -std::string chainID_
        +Name() NameType
        +FirstAtom() int
        +LastAtom() int
        +OriginalResNum() int
    }

    class Molecule {
        -Unit mol_unit_
        -bool solvent_
        +MolUnit() Unit
        +IsSolvent() bool
        +SetSolvent(bool)
        +NumAtoms() int
    }

    Topology "1" --* "many" Atom : contains
    Topology "1" --* "many" Residue : contains
    Topology "1" --* "many" Molecule : contains
```

Sources: [src/Topology.h:16-364](), [src/Atom.h:7-129](), [src/ParameterTypes.h:1-624]()

## Core Data Structures

### Atoms

The Atom class is the basic building block of a Topology. Each atom contains information about its name, type, element, mass, charge, and bonding partners.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Atom {
        -double charge_
        -double polar_
        -double mass_
        -double gb_radius_
        -double gb_screen_
        -NameType aname_
        -NameType atype_
        -int atype_index_
        -AtomicElementType element_
        -int resnum_
        -int mol_
        -std::vector~int~ bonds_
        +Name() NameType
        +Type() NameType
        +Charge() double
        +Mass() double
        +Element() AtomicElementType
        +AtomicNumber() int
        +ResNum() int
        +MolNum() int
        +AddBondToIdx(int)
        +RemoveBondToIdx(int)
        +IsBondedTo(int) bool
    }
```

Atoms in CPPTRAJ store their element type using the `AtomicElementType` enumeration, which includes common elements like HYDROGEN, CARBON, NITROGEN, etc. This element information is used to determine bond lengths, radii, and other properties.

Sources: [src/Atom.h:7-129](), [src/Atom.cpp:1-760]()

### Residues

Residues represent groups of atoms that form a chemical unit (e.g., amino acids, nucleotides, small molecules). A residue defines its boundaries by storing the indices of its first and last atoms.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Residue Structure"
        R1["Residue"]
        A1["FirstAtom"]
        A2["LastAtom"]
        R1 -->|"FirstAtom()"| A1
        R1 -->|"LastAtom()"| A2
    end
```

Each residue stores:

- Name: Residue name (e.g., "GLY", "ALA")
- First and last atom indices: Define the residue boundaries
- Original residue number: From the input file
- Chain ID: PDB chain identifier
- Insertion code: PDB insertion code

Sources: [src/Topology.h:90-97](), [src/Topology.cpp:425-437]()

### Molecules

Molecules are collections of atoms connected by bonds. They are determined automatically based on bond connectivity when a topology is loaded or can be explicitly defined.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Molecule Organization"
        M["Molecule"]
        U["Unit (Atom Indices)"]
        S["IsSolvent() flag"]
        M --> U
        M --> S
    end
```

CPPTRAJ can identify solvent molecules based on naming conventions or explicitly through the `SetSolvent()` method. This distinction is important for many analyses that treat solvent differently from solute.

Sources: [src/Topology.h:99-106](), [src/Topology.cpp:140-176]()

### Bonds, Angles, and Dihedrals

The topology contains information about bonds, angles, and dihedrals (both involving hydrogen and not involving hydrogen):

| Container | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `bonds_` | Bonds not involving hydrogen |
| `bondsh_` | Bonds involving hydrogen |
| `angles_` | Angles not involving hydrogen |
| `anglesh_` | Angles involving hydrogen |
| `dihedrals_` | Dihedrals not involving hydrogen |
| `dihedralsh_` | Dihedrals involving hydrogen |

Each bond, angle, and dihedral stores the indices of the involved atoms and an index into parameter arrays that hold force constants and equilibrium values.

Sources: [src/Topology.h:110-146](), [src/ParameterTypes.h:22-252]()

### Parameter Sets

Topology contains force field parameters for bonds, angles, dihedrals, and non-bonded interactions:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Parameter Organization"
        P["Topology Parameters"]
        BP["BondParmArray"] 
        AP["AngleParmArray"]
        DP["DihedralParmArray"]
        NB["NonbondParmType"]
        P --> BP
        P --> AP
        P --> DP
        P --> NB
    end
```

The parameters include:
- Bond parameters: Force constants and equilibrium bond lengths
- Angle parameters: Force constants and equilibrium angles
- Dihedral parameters: Force constants, periodicity, and phase values
- Non-bonded parameters: Lennard-Jones parameters for atom type pairs

Sources: [src/Topology.h:154-166](), [src/ParameterTypes.h:253-449]()

## Key Functionality

### Creating and Modifying Topologies

There are several ways to create or modify a Topology:

1. Reading from files (via `Parm_Amber` and other format readers)
2. Adding atoms, residues, and bonds manually
3. Modifying an existing topology (stripping atoms, merging residues, etc.)

Key methods for modifying a topology include:

- `AddTopAtom()`: Add a new atom to the topology
- `AddBond()`: Add a bond between two atoms
- `AddAngle()`: Add an angle between three atoms
- `AddDihedral()`: Add a dihedral between four atoms
- `MergeResidues()`: Merge consecutive residues into a single residue

Sources: [src/Topology.cpp:420-437](), [src/Topology.cpp:824-891](), [src/Topology.cpp:924-954]()

### Topology Analysis and Information Retrieval

Topology provides methods to access and analyze its components:

- `Natom()`, `Nres()`, `Nmol()`: Get count of atoms, residues, molecules
- `SoluteResidues()`: Get range of solute residues
- `FindAtomInResidue()`: Find atom within a specific residue
- `DetermineMolecules()`: Analyze bonds to determine molecule information
- `Summary()`, `Brief()`: Print information about the topology

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Molecule Determination"
        direction LR
        T["Topology"] 
        BL["Bond Lists in Atoms"]
        MB["Molecules Based on Connectivity"]
        T -->|"Use bond information"| BL
        BL -->|"Group connected atoms"| MB
        MB -->|"Store in molecules_"| T
    end
```

The `DetermineMolecules()` method analyzes bond connectivity to divide atoms into distinct molecules. This is important for analyses that need to know about molecular boundaries.

Sources: [src/Topology.cpp:267-293](), [src/Topology.cpp:358-417]()

### Atom Selection and Masking

The Topology class provides methods to set up atom masks, which are used throughout CPPTRAJ to select subsets of atoms for analysis:

- `SetupIntegerMask()`: Set up an AtomMask using this topology
- `SetupCharMask()`: Set up a CharMask using this topology

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Atom Mask Setup"
        T["Topology"]
        M["AtomMask (with mask expression)"]
        S["Selected Atoms"]
        
        T -->|"SetupIntegerMask()"| M
        M -->|"Contains selection"| S
    end
```

These methods parse mask expressions (like `:1-10` or `@CA`) and select the appropriate atoms based on the topology information.

Sources: [src/Topology.h:223-233]()

## Integration with Other Components

### Topology and Frame

Topology works closely with the Frame class, which stores the actual coordinate data. A Frame without a corresponding Topology lacks context about what the coordinates represent.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Topology and Frame Relationship"
        T["Topology"]
        F["Frame"]
        A["Atoms"]
        C["Coordinates"]
        T -->|"Contains info about"| A
        F -->|"Contains positions for"| C
        A ---o C
    end
```

The Topology provides the structural context (what atoms are where, how they're connected), while the Frame provides the spatial information (where atoms are in 3D space).

Sources: [src/Topology.h:209-211]()

### Topology in the CPPTRAJ Workflow

In the broader CPPTRAJ architecture, Topology is central to many operations:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Topology in CPPTRAJ"
        direction TB
        
        Input["Input Files"]
        TopRead["ParmIO Classes (e.g., Parm_Amber)"]
        Top["Topology"]
        Traj["Trajectory Files"]
        Frame["Frame Data"]
        Actions["Actions"]
        Analysis["Analyses"]
        
        Input -->|"Read"| TopRead
        TopRead -->|"Create"| Top
        Traj -->|"Read with context from"| Top
        Traj -->|"Populate"| Frame
        Top -->|"Provide context for"| Actions
        Frame -->|"Provide coordinates for"| Actions
        Top -->|"Provide structure for"| Analysis
    end
```

The Topology is created from input files, then provides context for trajectories, actions, and analyses throughout CPPTRAJ.

Sources: High-Level System Architecture diagram, Trajectory Handling section, Data Flow Architecture diagram provided in the context.

## Special Features

### PDB-Specific Information

Topology can store PDB-specific information such as alternate locations, B-factors, occupancies, and original atom numbering. These details are preserved when reading from and writing to PDB files.

Sources: [src/Topology.h:65-89](), [src/Topology.cpp:52-70]()

### Non-Standard Force Field Support

Topology supports specialized force field features:

- CHAMBER parameters for CHARMM force fields
- LES (Locally Enhanced Sampling) parameters
- CMAP (Correction Map) for improved protein backbone energetics
- Water cap information

Sources: [src/Topology.h:169-179](), [src/ParameterTypes.h:450-622]()

## Common Operations

### Determining Bond Connectivity

When bond parameters aren't available, CPPTRAJ can estimate them based on elemental types:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Bond Parameter Assignment"
        A1["Atom 1"]
        A2["Atom 2"]
        E1["Element Type 1"]
        E2["Element Type 2"]
        BL["Bond Length"]
        BP["Bond Parameter"]
        
        A1 -->|"Get element"| E1
        A2 -->|"Get element"| E2
        E1 --> BL
        E2 --> BL
        BL -->|"Create"| BP
    end
```

The `AssignBondParameters()` method uses atom elements to determine appropriate bond lengths when they're not explicitly provided in the input file.

Sources: [src/Topology.cpp:736-745](), [src/Atom.cpp:624-739]()

### Solvent Identification

CPPTRAJ can automatically identify solvent molecules based on residue naming or explicit marking:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Solvent Identification"
        M["Molecule"]
        R["Residue Name"]
        C["Criteria (e.g., 'HOH')"]
        S["Set IsSolvent flag"]
        
        M -->|"Check"| R
        R -->|"Compare to"| C
        C -->|"If matches"| S
        S -->|"Mark"| M
    end
```

Methods like `SetSolventInfo()` and `SetSolvent()` are used to identify and mark solvent molecules, which is important for many analyses that treat solvent differently.

Sources: [src/Topology.cpp:140-176](), [src/Topology.cpp:565-570]()

## Summary

The Topology class is a central component in CPPTRAJ that holds all the structural and parametric information about a molecular system. It manages atoms, residues, molecules, and their connectivity, providing context for trajectory processing and analysis. Understanding the Topology class is essential for effectively using CPPTRAJ and extending its functionality.

# Page: Frame

# Frame

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/Action_AtomicFluct.cpp](src/Action_AtomicFluct.cpp)
- [src/Action_AtomicFluct.h](src/Action_AtomicFluct.h)
- [src/Action_Average.cpp](src/Action_Average.cpp)
- [src/Action_Average.h](src/Action_Average.h)
- [src/Action_Outtraj.cpp](src/Action_Outtraj.cpp)
- [src/Action_Outtraj.h](src/Action_Outtraj.h)
- [src/AtomMask.cpp](src/AtomMask.cpp)
- [src/AtomMask.h](src/AtomMask.h)
- [src/Frame.cpp](src/Frame.cpp)
- [src/Frame.h](src/Frame.h)

</details>



## Introduction

The Frame class is a fundamental data structure in the CPPTRAJ system that holds atomic coordinates and related information for molecular systems. It serves as the primary container for processing trajectories, performing coordinate transformations, and calculating structural properties.

Frame is designed to efficiently store and manipulate coordinates, along with optional velocity and force data, and provides functionality for transformations like translations and rotations, as well as analysis operations like RMSD calculations.

Sources: [src/Frame.h:9-32]()

## Structure of the Frame Class

A Frame object contains several key components:

- **Coordinates**: 3D positions for all atoms in the system, stored as a contiguous array
- **Optional components**: Velocities and forces when available
- **Box information**: Unit cell dimensions and angles for periodic systems
- **Metadata**: Temperature, time, pH, step information, etc.
- **Mass information**: Mass of each atom used in various calculations

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Frame {
        -int natom_
        -int maxnatom_
        -int ncoord_
        -int step_
        -Box box_
        -double T_
        -double pH_
        -double time_
        -double* X_
        -double* V_
        -double* F_
        -std::vector~int~ remd_indices_
        -std::vector~double~ Mass_
        -bool memIsExternal_
        +Frame()
        +~Frame()
        +SetupFrame()
        +Translate()
        +Rotate()
        +RMSD()
        +VCenterOfMass()
    }

    class Box {
        -double* box_
        +SetBox()
        +GetBox()
    }

    Frame --> Box : contains
```

Sources: [src/Frame.h:287-306](), [src/Frame.h:34-593]()

## Frame in the CPPTRAJ Architecture

The Frame class is a core component of the CPPTRAJ Trajectory Handling subsystem, serving as the central data structure for coordinate manipulation throughout the program.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "CPPTRAJ System"
        Traj["Trajectory Files"] --> TrajIO["Trajectory I/O"]
        TrajIO --> Frame["Frame"]
        Frame --> ActionList["Action List"]
        Frame --> Analysis["Analysis"]
        
        AtomMask["AtomMask"] --> Frame
        Box["Box"] --> Frame
        
        Frame --> Output["Output Files"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Frame Operations"
        Transform["Coordinate Transformations"]
        Calculate["Property Calculations"]
        Measure["Structural Measurements"]
    end
    
    Frame --> Transform
    Frame --> Calculate
    Frame --> Measure
```

Sources: [src/Frame.h:9-32](), [src/Frame.cpp:3-6]()

## Memory Management

Frame employs careful memory management to handle coordinate data efficiently:

1. **Internal vs External Memory**:
   - Frames can own their memory (internal) or reference external memory
   - The `memIsExternal_` flag tracks this distinction
   - Only internally managed memory is freed in the destructor

2. **Dynamic Resizing**:
   - The class maintains `maxnatom_` to track the maximum capacity
   - When more space is needed, methods like `IncreaseX()` allocate larger arrays

3. **Memory Layout**:
   - Coordinates are stored in a flat array as X₁Y₁Z₁X₂Y₂Z₂...
   - This layout enables efficient memory operations and interfacing with file I/O

Sources: [src/Frame.cpp:29-36](), [src/Frame.cpp:307-318](), [src/Frame.h:285-306]()

## Frame Construction and Setup

The Frame class offers multiple constructors and setup methods to accommodate different use cases:

### Constructors

- **Default constructor**: Creates an empty frame
- **Size constructor**: Creates a frame for a given number of atoms
- **Atom-based constructor**: Initializes from a vector of Atom objects
- **Mask-based constructor**: Creates a frame with selected atoms from another frame
- **External memory constructor**: Creates a frame that references external coordinate data

### Setup Methods

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Empty["Empty Frame"] --> Setup["SetupFrame()"]
    Setup --> Basic["Basic Frame\nCoordinates Only"]
    
    Empty --> SetupM["SetupFrameM()"]
    SetupM --> WithMass["Frame with Masses"]
    
    Empty --> SetupV["SetupFrameV()"]
    SetupV --> Full["Complete Frame\nCoords, Mass, Velocities"]
    
    Empty --> SetupMask["SetupFrameFromMask()"]
    SetupMask --> Selected["Selected Atoms Only"]
```

Sources: [src/Frame.cpp:11-158](), [src/Frame.cpp:390-508](), [src/Frame.h:145-160]()

## Coordinate Access and Manipulation

Frame provides numerous methods to access and manipulate coordinates:

### Coordinate Access

- Direct access through operators: `frame[idx]`
- Atom-specific access: `XYZ(atom_num)` returns pointer to x,y,z coordinates for a given atom
- System information access: `Natom()`, `Temperature()`, `BoxCrd()`, etc.

### Coordinate Manipulation

The class offers comprehensive methods for common coordinate operations:

1. **Translations**
   - Whole system: `Translate()`, `NegTranslate()`
   - Atom subsets: `Translate(mask)`, `Translate(begin, end)`
   
2. **Rotations**
   - Whole system: `Rotate(matrix)`, `InverseRotate(matrix)`
   - Atom subsets: `Rotate(matrix, mask)`
   
3. **Combined Operations**
   - `Trans_Rot_Trans()`: Translation, rotation, and a second translation

Sources: [src/Frame.h:440-592](), [src/Frame.cpp:472-574]()

## Structural Calculations

Frame implements various methods for structural analysis:

1. **Center Calculations**
   - `VCenterOfMass()`: Calculate center of mass
   - `VGeometricCenter()`: Calculate geometric center
   - Variants for different atom selections

2. **RMSD Calculations**
   - `RMSD()`: Calculate RMSD between frames
   - `RMSD_CenteredRef()`: RMSD to a previously centered reference
   - `RMSD_NoFit()`: RMSD without structural alignment

3. **Other Analysis**
   - `VMomentum()`: Calculate momentum
   - `CalcTemperature()`: Calculate temperature

Sources: [src/Frame.h:214-269](), [src/Frame.cpp:1022-1207]()

## Coordinate Array Structure

The coordinate array in Frame is organized as a contiguous block of memory for performance reasons:

```
X_[0]   X_[1]   X_[2]   X_[3]   X_[4]   X_[5]   ...
X₁      Y₁      Z₁      X₂      Y₂      Z₂      ...
```

This layout provides:
- Efficient memory access patterns
- Straightforward interfacing with external libraries
- Simple pointer arithmetic for atom access

Access to coordinates is typically done via methods that calculate the appropriate offset:
- `XYZ(atom)` returns a pointer to the coordinates of the specified atom
- When iterating through atom masks, the coordinates are accessed via `X_ + (*atom * 3)`

Sources: [src/Frame.h:84-86](), [src/Frame.cpp:580-583]()

## Frame Manipulation with AtomMask

The AtomMask class is frequently used with Frame to operate on subsets of atoms:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Frame["Frame\n(All Atoms)"] --> Operation["Frame Operation\n(with Mask)"]
    AtomMask["AtomMask\n(Selected Atoms)"] --> Operation
    Operation --> Result["Result\n(Selected Atoms Only)"]
```

Common operations using AtomMask include:
- Creating a new Frame from a subset of atoms: `Frame(frameIn, maskIn)`
- Setting coordinates based on a mask: `SetCoordinates(frameIn, maskIn)`
- Manipulating specific atoms: `Translate(Vec, maskIn)`, `Rotate(Matrix, maskIn)`
- Calculating properties: `VCenterOfMass(maskIn)`, `RMSD(frameIn, maskIn)`

Sources: [src/Frame.cpp:86-140](), [src/Frame.cpp:561-574](), [src/AtomMask.h:5-90]()

## Usage Examples

The Frame class is used extensively throughout CPPTRAJ. Here are some common usage patterns:

### Creating and Setting Up a Frame

```
// Create a frame for a specific number of atoms
Frame coords(natoms);

// Set up a frame for selected atoms
AtomMask mask(":1-10");  // Residues 1-10
parm.SetupIntegerMask(mask);
Frame selectedAtoms;
selectedAtoms.SetupFrameFromMask(mask, parm.Atoms());
```

### Computing Properties

```
// Calculate center of mass
AtomMask proteinMask(":1-100");
Vec3 center = frame.VCenterOfMass(proteinMask);

// Calculate RMSD between frames
double rmsd = frame.RMSD(reference, true); // true = use mass-weighting
```

### Applying Transformations

```
// Translate atoms
Vec3 translation(1.0, 0.0, 0.0);  // Move 1Å along x-axis
frame.Translate(translation);

// Rotate atoms
Matrix_3x3 rotation;
rotation.RotationMatrix(Vec3(0,0,1), 45.0);  // 45° around z-axis
frame.Rotate(rotation);
```

## Action Usage Examples

Several CPPTRAJ actions use Frame as their core data structure:

### Atomic Fluctuations

The `AtomicFluct` action calculates atomic fluctuations by accumulating coordinate sums and variances in Frame objects:

```
SumCoords_.SetupFrame(Mask_.Nselected());   // For average positions
SumCoords2_.SetupFrame(Mask_.Nselected());  // For squared positions
```

Sources: [src/Action_AtomicFluct.cpp:123-126](), [src/Action_AtomicFluct.h:22-26]()

### Coordinate Averaging

The `Average` action uses Frame to accumulate and average coordinates:

```
AvgFrame_.SetupFrame(Mask_.Nselected());
AvgFrame_.ZeroCoords();
AvgFrame_.AddByMask(frm.Frm(), Mask_);  // Add coordinates from current frame
// Later:
AvgFrame_.Divide(double(Nframes_));     // Divide by number of frames
```

Sources: [src/Action_Average.cpp:93-94](), [src/Action_Average.cpp:135-136](), [src/Action_Average.h:25-26]()

## Summary

The Frame class is a core component of CPPTRAJ that:
- Efficiently stores atomic coordinates, velocities, forces, and related information
- Provides methods for coordinate manipulation and structural analysis
- Interfaces with other key components like AtomMask for atom selection
- Forms the foundation for many analysis actions in the CPPTRAJ system

Understanding Frame is essential for working with trajectory data in CPPTRAJ, as it forms the central data structure around which much of the system's functionality is built.

---

# Data Management

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/DataFile.cpp](src/DataFile.cpp)

</details>



This page documents the data management system in CPPTRAJ, which is responsible for storing, organizing, and handling various types of data throughout the application. This includes how data is represented in memory, how it's organized into collections, and how it's written to and read from files.

The data management system provides a flexible framework that supports numerous data types (from simple scalars to complex matrices and coordinates) and file formats (standard text, Grace, Gnuplot, etc.). It serves as the central data handling backbone for the entire application, bridging trajectory processing with analysis and output.

For information on trajectory input/output, see [Trajectory Handling](#3.2).

## Core Data Management Classes

The data management system in CPPTRAJ consists of several key classes that work together to provide a flexible and extensible framework:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DataSet {
        <<abstract>>
        +DataType Type()
        +DataGroup Group()
        +MetaData Meta()
        +Size()
        +Ndim()
        +WriteBuffer()
    }
    
    class DataSetList {
        -vector~DataSet*~ DataList_
        -bool hasCopies_
        -bool dataSetsPending_
        +AddSet()
        +GetDataSet()
        +FindSetOfType()
        +SelectSets()
        +RemoveSet()
    }
    
    class DataFile {
        -DataSetList SetList_
        -DataIO* dataio_
        -DataFormatType dfType_
        -FileName filename_
        +AddDataSet()
        +WriteDataOut()
        +SetDataFilePrecision()
    }
    
    class DataFileList {
        -vector~DataFile*~ fileList_
        -vector~CpptrajFile*~ cfList_
        +AddDataFile()
        +WriteAllDF()
        +GetDataFile()
        +RemoveDataSet()
    }
    
    class DataIO {
        <<abstract>>
        +ReadData()
        +WriteData()
        +processReadArgs()
        +processWriteArgs()
    }
    
    DataSetList --> "0..n" DataSet : contains
    DataFile --> DataSetList : contains
    DataFile --> "1" DataIO : uses
    DataFileList --> "0..n" DataFile : contains
    DataFileList --> "0..n" CpptrajFile : contains
```

Sources: [src/DataSet.h:13-166](). [src/DataSetList.h:12-205](). [src/DataFile.h:8-125](). [src/DataFileList.h:8-113](). [src/DataIO.h:8-58]().

### DataSet

`DataSet` is the base class for all data types in CPPTRAJ. It's an abstract class that defines the interface for storing and accessing various types of data. Each `DataSet` contains metadata, dimension information, and the actual data values.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DataSet {
        <<abstract>>
        +MetaData Meta()
        +Dimension Dim()
        +TextFormat Format()
        +DataType Type()
        +DataGroup Group()
        +Size()
        +Ndim()
        +Add()
        +Allocate()
        +WriteBuffer()
    }
    
    class DataSet_1D {
        <<abstract>>
        +Dval()
        +Xvals()
    }
    
    class DataSet_2D {
        <<abstract>>
        +Allocate2D()
        +GetElement()
        +SetElement()
    }
    
    class DataSet_3D {
        <<abstract>>
        +Allocate3D()
        +GetElement()
        +SetElement()
    }
    
    class DataSet_double {
        -vector~double~ Data_
        +AddElement()
        +operator[]()
    }
    
    class DataSet_string {
        -vector~string~ Data_
        +AddElement()
        +operator[]()
    }
    
    class DataSet_MatrixDbl {
        -vector~double~ Data_
        -size_t ncols_
        -size_t nrows_
        +AllocateMatrix()
        +operator()
    }
    
    DataSet <|-- DataSet_1D
    DataSet <|-- DataSet_2D
    DataSet <|-- DataSet_3D
    DataSet_1D <|-- DataSet_double
    DataSet_1D <|-- DataSet_string
    DataSet_2D <|-- DataSet_MatrixDbl
```

Sources: [src/DataSet.h:13-166](). [src/DataSet.cpp:1-144]().

DataSets are categorized by both type and group:

1. **DataSet::DataType** - Specific data type (e.g., DOUBLE, STRING, MATRIX_DBL)
2. **DataSet::DataGroup** - General category (e.g., SCALAR_1D, MATRIX_2D, GRID_3D)

This dual categorization provides flexibility when searching for and operating on DataSets.

### DataSetList

`DataSetList` is a container class that manages collections of `DataSet` objects. It provides methods for adding, finding, and manipulating DataSets.

Key features of the DataSetList include:

- Adding DataSets of various types
- Finding DataSets by name, type, group, or other attributes
- Selecting multiple DataSets based on criteria
- Managing special types of DataSets (reference frames, topologies)
- Allocating memory for time series data

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "DataSetList Operations"
        A("AddSet()") --> |"Create New"| D["DataSet"]
        F("FindSetOfType()") --> |"Search"| D
        G("GetMultipleSets()") --> |"Return List"| D2["DataSets"]
        S("SelectSets()") --> |"Filter"| D2
        R("RemoveSet()") --> |"Delete"| D
    end
    
    subgraph "Special Management"
        REF["Reference Sets"]
        TOP["Topology Sets"]
        VAR["String Variables"]
        M1["GetReferenceFrame()"]
        M2["GetTopology()"]
        M3["UpdateStringVar()"]
    end
    
    D --> REF
    D --> TOP
    D --> VAR
```

Sources: [src/DataSetList.h:12-205](). [src/DataSetList.cpp:1-141](). [src/DataSetList.cpp:142-282](). [src/DataSetList.cpp:283-422](). [src/DataSetList.cpp:840-953]().

### DataFile and DataIO

`DataFile` handles the writing of DataSets to files in various formats. It uses `DataIO` objects to perform the actual file I/O operations.

`DataIO` is an abstract base class for file I/O operations. Different file formats have their own `DataIO` implementations:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DataIO {
        <<abstract>>
        +ReadData()
        +WriteData()
        +processReadArgs()
        +processWriteArgs()
    }
    
    class DataIO_Std {
        +Read_1D()
        +Read_2D()
        +Read_3D()
        +WriteDataNormal()
    }
    
    class DataIO_Grace {
        +WriteDataNormal()
        +WriteDataXYDY()
        +WriteDataInverted()
    }
    
    class DataIO_Gnuplot {
        +WriteSets1D()
        +WriteSet2D()
    }
    
    class DataIO_Mdout {
        +GetAmberEterms()
    }
    
    DataIO <|-- DataIO_Std
    DataIO <|-- DataIO_Grace
    DataIO <|-- DataIO_Gnuplot
    DataIO <|-- DataIO_Mdout
    DataIO <|-- DataIO_XYZ["Many Others..."]
```

Sources: [src/DataIO.h:8-58](). [src/DataIO.cpp:1-122](). [src/DataIO_Std.h:5-65](). [src/DataIO_Grace.h:4-25](). [src/DataIO_Gnuplot.h:5-52](). [src/DataIO_Mdout.h:6-35]().

`DataFile` wraps a `DataIO` implementation and provides a higher-level interface:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["DataFile"] -->|"contains"| B["DataSetList"]
    A -->|"uses"| C["DataIO"]
    
    A -->|"AddDataSet()"| D["Add DataSet to file"]
    A -->|"SetDataFilePrecision()"| E["Set output precision"]
    A -->|"WriteDataOut()"| F["Write data to disk"]
    
    subgraph "Data Output Process"
        F -->|"if ensExt_"| G["WriteWithEnsExtension()"]
        F -->|"else"| H["WriteNoEnsExtension()"]
        G -->|"for each ensemble"| I["WriteSetsToFile()"]
        H -->|"all sets together"| I
        I -->|"uses"| J["dataio_->WriteData()"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.h:8-125](). [src/DataFile.cpp:39-172](). [src/DataFile.cpp:173-346](). [src/DataFile.cpp:347-520](). [src/DataFile.cpp:521-669]().

### DataFileList

`DataFileList` manages collections of `DataFile` objects and `CpptrajFile` objects (for text output). It ensures that multiple data sets can be directed to the same file and coordinates writing all files at appropriate times.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["DataFileList"] -->|"contains"| B["DataFiles"]
    A -->|"contains"| C["CpptrajFiles"]
    
    A -->|"AddDataFile()"| D["Create/Find DataFile"]
    A -->|"AddCpptrajFile()"| E["Create/Find CpptrajFile"]
    A -->|"WriteAllDF()"| F["Write all pending DataFiles"]
    
    subgraph "File Operations"
        F -->|"for each DataFile"| G["if DFLwrite"]
        G -->|"true"| H["WriteDataOut()"]
        H --> I["Set DFLwrite to false"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/DataFileList.h:8-113](). [src/DataFileList.cpp:11-99](). [src/DataFileList.cpp:100-210](). [src/DataFileList.cpp:343-380]().

## DataSet Types and Hierarchies

CPPTRAJ supports a wide variety of data types, organized in a hierarchical manner. Each DataSet has both a type and a group categorization.

### DataSet Types

The `DataSet::DataType` enumeration defines all possible data types:

```
DOUBLE         - Double precision floating point
FLOAT          - Single precision floating point
INTEGER        - Integer values
STRING         - String values
MATRIX_DBL     - Double precision matrices
MATRIX_FLT     - Single precision matrices
COORDS         - Coordinate data
VECTOR         - Vector data
MODES          - Eigenmodes
GRID_FLT       - Single precision grids
GRID_DBL       - Double precision grids
REMLOG         - Replica exchange logs
XYMESH         - XY mesh data
TRAJ           - Trajectory data
REF_FRAME      - Reference frames
MAT3X3         - 3x3 matrices
TOPOLOGY       - Topology data
PH             - pH data
...and more
```

Sources: [src/DataSet.h:26-34](). [src/DataSet.cpp:6-37]().

### DataSet Groups

The `DataSet::DataGroup` enumeration defines broader categories:

```
GENERIC        - Generic data not fitting other categories
SCALAR_1D      - One-dimensional scalar data
MATRIX_2D      - Two-dimensional matrix data
GRID_3D        - Three-dimensional grid data
COORDINATES    - Coordinate data sets
PHREMD         - pH replica exchange data
PWCACHE        - Pairwise caches
VECTOR_1D      - One-dimensional vector data
```

Sources: [src/DataSet.h:36-37]().

## Data File Formats

CPPTRAJ supports numerous file formats for data input and output through the `DataIO` class hierarchy:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["DataFile"] -->|"Uses"| B["DataIO"]
    
    B -->|"Formats"| C["Standard Text"]
    B -->|"Formats"| D["Grace"]
    B -->|"Formats"| E["Gnuplot"]
    B -->|"Formats"| F["Xplor"]
    B -->|"Formats"| G["OpenDX"]
    B -->|"Formats"| H["AMBER Outputs"]
    B -->|"Formats"| I["NetCDF"]
    B -->|"Formats"| J["...and more"]
    
    C --> C1["Column-based data"]
    D --> D1["XY plots"]
    E --> E1["Gnuplot scripts/data"]
    F --> F1["Grid/volume data"]
    H --> H1["MDOUT, REMLOG, etc."]
    I --> I1["Binary HDF5/NetCDF"]
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.h:17-22](). [src/DataFile.cpp:59-93](). [src/DataIO_Std.h:5-65](). [src/DataIO_Grace.h:4-25](). [src/DataIO_Gnuplot.h:5-52]().

The format used is determined by:
1. Explicit specification in commands
2. File extension
3. Automatic detection by content (for reading)

## DataSet Creation and Management

DataSets are primarily created and managed through the `DataSetList` class.

### Creating DataSets

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["DataSetList"] -->|"AddSet()"| B["Allocate memory"]
    B --> C["Set MetaData"]
    C --> D["Return DataSet pointer"]
    
    A -->|"AllocateSet()"| E["Create without adding to list"]
    
    A -->|"AddOrAppendSets()"| F["Handle data from files"]
    F -->|"if exists"| G["Append to existing set"]
    F -->|"if new"| H["Create new set"]
```

Sources: [src/DataSetList.cpp:424-578](). [src/DataSetList.cpp:579-696]().

### Finding DataSets

DataSets can be located in multiple ways:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["DataSetList"] -->|"GetDataSet(nameIn)"| B["Find one set by name"]
    A -->|"SelectSets(nameIn)"| C["Find multiple sets by name"]
    A -->|"FindSetOfType(name, type)"| D["Find by name and type"]
    A -->|"SelectGroupSets(name, group)"| E["Find by name and group"]
    
    B --> F["Name match (exact)"]
    C --> G["Wildcard matching"]
    D --> H["Type and name match"]
    E --> I["Group and name match"]
    
    F --> J["MetaData::Match_Exact()"]
    G --> K["MetaData::Match_WildCard()"]
```

Sources: [src/DataSetList.cpp:298-410]().

### DataSet MetaData

The `MetaData` class stores information about each DataSet, including:

- Name - Primary identifier
- Aspect - Secondary qualifier
- Index - Numerical qualifier 
- Legend - Display name
- Ensemble number - For ensemble simulations

This metadata system provides a flexible way to identify and organize data sets within the application.

## Data Output Process

When data is written, the process follows this flow:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Action as "Action or Analysis"
    participant DSL as "DataSetList"
    participant DFL as "DataFileList"
    participant DF as "DataFile"
    participant DIO as "DataIO"
    
    Action->>DSL: Create DataSet
    Action->>DFL: AddDataFile(filename)
    DFL-->>Action: DataFile pointer
    Action->>DF: AddDataSet(dataSet)
    
    Note over DFL: Later, during finalization
    
    DFL->>DF: WriteDataOut()
    DF->>DF: Organize sets by ensemble
    DF->>DIO: WriteData(filename, sets)
    DIO->>DIO: Format-specific writing
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.cpp:610-629](). [src/DataFileList.cpp:364-380]().

## Ensemble Data Management

CPPTRAJ provides special handling for ensemble data:

1. DataSets can have ensemble number metadata
2. DataFiles can write ensemble data to separate files
3. Ensemble member numbers can be appended to filenames

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["DataFileList"] -->|"ensembleExt_"| B{"Use member extensions?"}
    B -->|"Yes"| C["Append .X to output files"]
    B -->|"No"| D["Write as single file"]
    
    E["DataFile"] -->|"ensExt_"| F{"Write with extensions?"}
    F -->|"Yes"| G["WriteWithEnsExtension()"]
    F -->|"No"| H["WriteNoEnsExtension()"]
    
    G -->|"Separate files"| I["filename.0, filename.1, etc."]
    H -->|"Single file"| J["All data in one file"]
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.cpp:553-608](). [src/DataFileList.cpp:155-280]().

## Error Handling and Status Management

The data management system includes various mechanisms for tracking status and handling errors:

- `dflWrite_` flag in DataFile indicates files that need to be written
- `dataSetsPending_` in DataSetList signals when Actions will create sets later
- Return codes from read/write operations indicate success or failure
- Debug output can be enabled at various levels

Each component also provides its own error reporting through the `mprintf()` and `mprinterr()` functions.

## Example Data Flow

A typical data flow in CPPTRAJ might look like this:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Command Input"] -->|"CreateDataSet"| B["DataSetList"]
    A -->|"CreateOutputFile"| C["DataFileList"]
    
    B -->|"AddSet()"| D["DataSet Creation"]
    C -->|"AddDataFile()"| E["DataFile Creation"]
    
    D -->|"Data Added"| F["DataSet"]
    E -->|"Sets Added"| G["DataFile"]
    
    F -->|"AddDataSet()"| G
    
    H["Analysis Action"] -->|"Process Data"| F
    I["Run Command"] -->|"WriteAllDF()"| C
    C -->|"WriteDataOut()"| G
    G -->|"WriteData()"| J["File on Disk"]
```

Sources: [src/DataSetList.cpp:424-578](). [src/DataFile.cpp:406-440](). [src/DataFileList.cpp:364-380]().

## Data Management Best Practices

When working with the CPPTRAJ data management system, consider these best practices:

1. Use appropriate DataSet types for your data
2. Set meaningful metadata for better organization and searching
3. Group related data sets into the same output files
4. Be aware of ensemble data handling when working with multiple trajectories
5. Use data file arguments to control output format, precision, labels, etc.

## Conclusion

The data management system in CPPTRAJ provides a flexible framework for storing, organizing, and outputting data from trajectory analysis. By understanding the relationships between DataSets, DataSetLists, DataFiles, DataFileList, and DataIO objects, you can effectively work with the various data types and formats supported by CPPTRAJ.

The CPPTRAJ file I/O system provides a unified framework for reading and writing molecular dynamics trajectory data in various file formats. This page documents the architecture of the file I/O system, how trajectory formats are detected, and the process of reading/writing trajectory data.

For information about how to use file I/O from the command line, see the user documentation. This page focuses on the internal implementation details for developers.

## File I/O Architecture

CPPTRAJ uses a factory pattern to handle different file formats. The system consists of a `TrajectoryFile` class that acts as a factory for creating format-specific `TrajectoryIO` instances.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class TrajectoryFile {
        +enum TrajFormatType
        +static DetectFormat(FileName const&, TrajFormatType&) TrajectoryIO*
        +static DetectFormat(FileName const&, std::string const&, TrajFormatType&) TrajectoryIO*
        +static AllocTrajIO(TrajFormatType) TrajectoryIO*
        +static ReadOptions(std::string const&) void
        +static WriteOptions(std::string const&) void
        -static const FileTypes::AllocToken TF_AllocArray[]
        -static const FileTypes::KeyToken TF_KeyArray[]
        -static const FileTypes::KeyToken TF_WriteKeyArray[]
    }
    class TrajectoryIO {
        +virtual bool ID_TrajFormat(CpptrajFile&)
        +virtual int setupTrajin(FileName const&, Topology*)
        +virtual int setupTrajout(FileName const&, Topology*, CoordinateInfo const&, int, bool)
        +virtual int openTrajin()
        +virtual void closeTraj()
        +virtual int readFrame(int, Frame&)
        +virtual int writeFrame(int, Frame const&)
        +virtual int readVelocity(int, Frame&)
        +virtual int readForce(int, Frame&)
        +virtual void Info()
    }
    class CpptrajFile {
        +int OpenFileRead(FileName const&)
        +int OpenFileWrite(FileName const&)
        +int OpenFile()
        +void CloseFile()
        +int Seek(long)
        +int Read(void*, size_t)
        +int Write(void*, size_t)
    }
    
    TrajectoryFile --> TrajectoryIO : creates
    TrajectoryIO --> CpptrajFile : uses
    
    class Traj_PDBfile {
        +PDBfile file_
        +bool ID_TrajFormat(CpptrajFile&)
        +int setupTrajin(FileName const&, Topology*)
        +int setupTrajout(FileName const&, Topology*, CoordinateInfo const&, int, bool)
        +int openTrajin()
        +void closeTraj()
        +int readFrame(int, Frame&)
        +int writeFrame(int, Frame const&)
    }
    class Traj_AmberNetcdf {
        +bool ID_TrajFormat(CpptrajFile&)
        +int setupTrajin(FileName const&, Topology*)
        +int setupTrajout(FileName const&, Topology*, CoordinateInfo const&, int, bool)
        +int openTrajin()
        +void closeTraj()
        +int readFrame(int, Frame&)
        +int writeFrame(int, Frame const&)
    }
    
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_PDBfile : implements
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_AmberNetcdf : implements
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_AmberRestart : implements
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_AmberRestartNC : implements
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_CharmmDcd : implements
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_AmberCoord : implements
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_Mol2File : implements
```

Sources: [src/TrajectoryFile.h:1-72](), [src/TrajectoryIO.h:1-73](), [src/Traj_PDBfile.h:1-99](), [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.h:1-40]()

### Key Classes

1. **TrajectoryFile**: Acts as a factory for creating `TrajectoryIO` instances based on file format. It contains static methods for format detection and allocation:
   - `DetectFormat()`: Determines the format of a trajectory file
   - `AllocTrajIO()`: Creates a `TrajectoryIO` instance for a specific format

2. **TrajectoryIO**: Abstract base class defining the interface for trajectory I/O operations. Key methods include:
   - `ID_TrajFormat()`: Identifies if a file matches this format
   - `setupTrajin()/setupTrajout()`: Prepares for reading/writing
   - `openTrajin()`: Opens a trajectory for reading
   - `readFrame()/writeFrame()`: Reads/writes a single frame
   - `closeTraj()`: Closes the trajectory

3. **Format-specific implementations**: Each supported file format has a corresponding class that inherits from `TrajectoryIO` and implements its methods. Examples include:
   - `Traj_PDBfile` for PDB files
   - `Traj_AmberNetcdf` for Amber NetCDF files
   - `Traj_AmberRestart` for Amber restart files
   - `Traj_CharmmDcd` for CHARMM DCD files

## Format Detection Process

When opening a trajectory, CPPTRAJ needs to determine its format. This is done by the `DetectFormat()` method in `TrajectoryFile`, which tries each registered format until one matches.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant TrajectoryFile
    participant CpptrajFile
    participant FormatA as "TrajectoryIO (FormatA)"
    participant FormatB as "TrajectoryIO (FormatB)"
    
    Client->>TrajectoryFile: DetectFormat(filename, type)
    TrajectoryFile->>CpptrajFile: SetupRead(filename)
    CpptrajFile-->>TrajectoryFile: Success
    TrajectoryFile->>FormatA: Alloc()
    FormatA-->>TrajectoryFile: FormatA instance
    TrajectoryFile->>FormatA: ID_TrajFormat(file)
    FormatA-->>TrajectoryFile: false
    TrajectoryFile->>FormatB: Alloc()
    FormatB-->>TrajectoryFile: FormatB instance
    TrajectoryFile->>FormatB: ID_TrajFormat(file)
    FormatB-->>TrajectoryFile: true
    TrajectoryFile-->>Client: FormatB instance, type=FormatB
```

Sources: [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:159-180](), [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:185-203]()

The format detection process uses three important arrays defined in `TrajectoryFile.cpp`:

1. **TF_AllocArray**: Maps format types to allocator functions and help text
2. **TF_KeyArray**: Maps format keywords and file extensions to format types for reading
3. **TF_WriteKeyArray**: Maps format keywords and file extensions to format types for writing

These arrays allow CPPTRAJ to:
- Create the appropriate `TrajectoryIO` object for a given format
- Recognize formats based on file extensions or format keywords
- Provide help text for read/write options specific to each format

## Reading Trajectories

Reading from a trajectory involves several steps:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant TrajectoryIO
    participant File
    
    Client->>TrajectoryIO: setupTrajin(filename, topology)
    TrajectoryIO->>File: SetupRead(filename)
    File-->>TrajectoryIO: Success
    TrajectoryIO->>File: OpenFile()
    File-->>TrajectoryIO: Success
    TrajectoryIO-->>Client: Number of frames
    Client->>TrajectoryIO: openTrajin()
    TrajectoryIO->>File: OpenFile()
    File-->>TrajectoryIO: Success
    TrajectoryIO-->>Client: Success
    Client->>TrajectoryIO: readFrame(frameNumber, frame)
    TrajectoryIO->>File: Seek(frameNumber)
    File-->>TrajectoryIO: Success
    TrajectoryIO->>File: Read(buffer)
    File-->>TrajectoryIO: Data
    TrajectoryIO-->>Client: Frame data
    Client->>TrajectoryIO: closeTraj()
    TrajectoryIO->>File: CloseFile()
    File-->>TrajectoryIO: Success
```

Sources: [src/Traj_PDBfile.cpp:81-178](), [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.cpp:61-103](), [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.cpp:180-231]()

The general process for reading trajectories is:

1. **setupTrajin()**: Sets up the trajectory for reading, determines the number of frames
2. **openTrajin()**: Opens the file for reading
3. **readFrame()**: Reads a specific frame from the trajectory
4. **closeTraj()**: Closes the file when done

Each format-specific implementation handles the details differently. For example, PDB files may need to handle TER records and multiple models, while NetCDF files need to interact with the NetCDF library.

## Writing Trajectories

Writing to a trajectory follows a similar pattern:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant TrajectoryIO
    participant File
    
    Client->>TrajectoryIO: setupTrajout(filename, topology, coordInfo, numFrames, append)
    TrajectoryIO->>File: SetupWrite(filename)
    File-->>TrajectoryIO: Success
    TrajectoryIO-->>Client: Success
    Client->>TrajectoryIO: writeFrame(frameNumber, frame)
    TrajectoryIO->>File: Write(buffer)
    File-->>TrajectoryIO: Success
    TrajectoryIO-->>Client: Success
    Client->>TrajectoryIO: closeTraj()
    TrajectoryIO->>File: CloseFile()
    File-->>TrajectoryIO: Success
```

Sources: [src/Traj_PDBfile.cpp:459-807](), [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.cpp:106-173](), [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.cpp:402-498]()

The general process for writing trajectories is:

1. **setupTrajout()**: Sets up the trajectory for writing, creates the file
2. **writeFrame()**: Writes a specific frame to the trajectory
3. **closeTraj()**: Closes the file and updates metadata when done

Writing also includes format-specific considerations. For instance, PDB files may need to handle ATOM vs. HETATM records, while NetCDF files need to define dimensions and variables before writing data.

## Supported File Formats

CPPTRAJ supports a wide range of file formats through the `TrajFormatType` enumeration in `TrajectoryFile`:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    FileFormats["Supported File Formats (TrajFormatType)"]
    FileFormats --> Amber["Amber Formats"]
    FileFormats --> PDB["PDB Format (PDBFILE)"]
    FileFormats --> CHARMM["CHARMM Formats"]

    CHARMM --> CharmmDcd["CHARMM DCD (CHARMMDCD)"]

    Gromacs --> GmxTrX["Gromacs TRX (GMXTRX)"]
    Gromacs --> GmxXtc["Gromacs XTC (GMXXTC)"]
    Gromacs --> GmxTng["Gromacs TNG (GMXTNG)"]
    Gromacs --> Gro["GRO file (GRO)"]
    Gromacs --> GmxDump["Gromacs Dump (GMXDUMP)"]

```

Sources: [src/TrajectoryFile.h:25-33](), [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:33-90](), [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:93-126](), [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:129-154]()

### Format Registration System

The format registration system in `TrajectoryFile.cpp` defines three key arrays:

1. **TF_AllocArray**: Maps format types to allocator functions and help text
   ```cpp
   const FileTypes::AllocToken TrajectoryFile::TF_AllocArray[] = {
     { "Amber NetCDF",       Traj_AmberNetcdf::ReadHelp, Traj_AmberNetcdf::WriteHelp, Traj_AmberNetcdf::Alloc    },
     { "Amber NC Restart",   Traj_AmberRestartNC::ReadHelp, Traj_AmberRestartNC::WriteHelp, Traj_AmberRestartNC::Alloc },
     // More formats...
   };
   ```

2. **TF_KeyArray**: Maps format keywords and file extensions to format types for reading
   ```cpp
   const FileTypes::KeyToken TrajectoryFile::TF_KeyArray[] = {
     { AMBERNETCDF,    "netcdf",    ".nc"      },
     { AMBERNETCDF,    "cdf",       ".nc"      },
     { AMBERRESTARTNC, "ncrestart", ".ncrst"   },
     // More mappings...
   };
   ```

3. **TF_WriteKeyArray**: Maps format keywords and file extensions to format types for writing
   ```cpp
   const FileTypes::KeyToken TrajectoryFile::TF_WriteKeyArray[] = {
     { AMBERNETCDF,    "netcdf",    ".nc"      },
     { AMBERNETCDF,    "cdf",       ".nc"      },
     { AMBERRESTARTNC, "ncrestart", ".ncrst"   },
     // More mappings...
   };
   ```

This registration system allows CPPTRAJ to:
- Create the appropriate `TrajectoryIO` object for a given format
- Recognize formats based on file extensions or format keywords
- Provide help text for read/write options specific to each format

## Format-Specific Details

### PDB Files

PDB files are handled by the `Traj_PDBfile` class. Key features include:
- Support for reading/writing standard PDB records (ATOM, HETATM, TER, etc.)
- Multiple write modes: single file, model records, or multiple files
- Options for handling B-factors, occupancy, and other PDB-specific fields

Sources: [src/Traj_PDBfile.cpp:13-42](), [src/Traj_PDBfile.cpp:233-266](), [src/Traj_PDBfile.cpp:268-383]()

### Amber NetCDF

Amber NetCDF files are handled by the `Traj_AmberNetcdf` class. Key features include:
- Support for coordinates, velocities, forces, and other data
- Compression options for HDF5/NetCDF4 files
- Options for temperature and time data

Sources: [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.cpp:17-46](), [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.cpp:72-74](), [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.cpp:98-173]()

### Amber Restart/Coordinates

Amber restart and coordinate files are handled by:
- `Traj_AmberRestart` for ASCII restart files
- `Traj_AmberRestartNC` for NetCDF restart files
- `Traj_AmberCoord` for Amber trajectory files

These formats support different combinations of coordinates, velocities, forces, and box information.

Sources: [src/Traj_AmberRestart.cpp:9-27](), [src/Traj_AmberRestartNC.cpp:14-33](), [src/Traj_AmberCoord.cpp:9-29]()

### CHARMM Formats

CHARMM formats include:
- `Traj_CharmmDcd` for DCD files
- `Traj_CharmmCor` for coordinate files
- `Traj_CharmmRest` for restart files

Sources: [src/Traj_CharmmDcd.cpp:12-36]()

## Implementation Details for Developers

When adding a new trajectory format to CPPTRAJ, you need to:

1. Create a new class that inherits from `TrajectoryIO`
2. Implement all required virtual methods
3. Add a unique entry to the `TrajFormatType` enum in `TrajectoryFile.h`
4. Add entries to the `TF_AllocArray`, `TF_KeyArray`, and `TF_WriteKeyArray` arrays in `TrajectoryFile.cpp`
5. Include the new class's header file in `TrajectoryFile.cpp`

### Required Virtual Methods

At a minimum, your new format class must implement:

```cpp
// Identify if a file matches this format
bool ID_TrajFormat(CpptrajFile&);

// Set up for reading
int setupTrajin(FileName const&, Topology*);

// Set up for writing
int setupTrajout(FileName const&, Topology*, CoordinateInfo const&, int, bool);

// Open file for reading
int openTrajin();

// Close file
void closeTraj();

// Read a frame
int readFrame(int, Frame&);

// Write a frame
int writeFrame(int, Frame const&);

// Print format info
void Info();
```

For more specialized formats, you may also need to implement `readVelocity()`, `readForce()`, and other methods.
