## Overview

This page documents the trajectory file formats supported by CPPTRAJ for reading and writing molecular dynamics (MD) trajectory data. CPPTRAJ supports a wide range of file formats, allowing interoperability with various MD software packages and enabling efficient analysis of simulation data.

For information about data file formats used for analysis results, see [Data File I/O](#5.2).

Sources: [src/TrajectoryFile.h:14-36]()

## Trajectory Format Architecture

CPPTRAJ uses a polymorphic architecture to handle different trajectory formats. Two primary classes form the foundation:

1. `TrajectoryFile`: Handles format detection and serves as a factory for creating appropriate I/O handlers
2. `TrajectoryIO`: Abstract base class that defines the interface for reading and writing trajectory data

Each supported format has its own implementation class derived from `TrajectoryIO`, providing format-specific reading and writing capabilities.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class TrajectoryFile {
        +enum TrajFormatType
        +static DetectFormat()
        +static ReadOptions()
        +static WriteOptions()
    }
    
    class TrajectoryIO {
        <<abstract>>
        +bool ID_TrajFormat(CpptrajFile&)
        +int setupTrajin(FileName const&, Topology*)
        +int setupTrajout(FileName const&, Topology*, CoordinateInfo const&, int, bool)
        +int readFrame(int, Frame&)
        +int writeFrame(int, Frame const&)
        +int readVelocity(int, Frame&)
        +int readForce(int, Frame&)
    }
    
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_AmberNetcdf
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_PDBfile
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_AmberRestart
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_CharmmDcd
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_Mol2File
    TrajectoryIO <|-- Traj_GmxXtc
    TrajectoryIO <|-- OtherFormats
    
    TrajectoryFile ..> TrajectoryIO : creates
    
    class OtherFormats {
        <<many other formats>>
    }
```

Sources: [src/TrajectoryFile.h:14-36](), [src/TrajectoryIO.h:23-43]()

### Format Detection Process

When a trajectory file is read, CPPTRAJ determines its format using the following process:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant TrajectoryFile
    participant FormatImplementation
    participant File

    User->>TrajectoryFile: DetectFormat(filename)
    TrajectoryFile->>File: Open file
    loop for each registered format
        TrajectoryFile->>FormatImplementation: Create implementation instance
        TrajectoryFile->>FormatImplementation: ID_TrajFormat(file)
        FormatImplementation->>File: Read header/check signature
        FormatImplementation-->>TrajectoryFile: Return format match result
        alt Format matches
            TrajectoryFile-->>User: Return implementation instance
            break
        else No match
            TrajectoryFile->>FormatImplementation: Delete instance
        end
    end
    TrajectoryFile-->>User: Return null if no match found
```

Sources: [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:158-203]()

## Supported Trajectory Formats

CPPTRAJ supports numerous trajectory file formats. The table below summarizes the most commonly used formats:

| Format | Extension | Read | Write | Coordinates | Velocities | Forces | Box | Description |
|--------|-----------|:----:|:-----:|:-----------:|:----------:|:------:|:---:|-------------|
| Amber NetCDF | .nc | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Binary NetCDF format with high precision |
| Amber Restart NetCDF | .ncrst | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | NetCDF-based restart format |
| Amber ASCII | .crd | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | Traditional ASCII coordinate format |
| Amber Restart | .rst7 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ASCII-based restart format |
| PDB | .pdb | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | Standard Protein Data Bank format |
| Mol2 | .mol2 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | Tripos Mol2 format |
| Charmm DCD | .dcd | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | Binary CHARMM trajectory format |
| Gromacs TRX | .trr | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Binary GROMACS trajectory |
| Gromacs XTC | .xtc | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | Compressed GROMACS trajectory |
| BINPOS | .binpos | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | Binary trajectory format |

Sources: [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:37-89](), [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:93-126](), [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:129-153]()

### Format Registration

Trajectory formats are registered in CPPTRAJ through three key static arrays in `TrajectoryFile.cpp`:

1. `TF_AllocArray`: Maps format types to allocation functions and help text
2. `TF_KeyArray`: Maps format keywords and file extensions to format types (for input)
3. `TF_WriteKeyArray`: Maps format keywords and file extensions to format types (for output)

Sources: [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:37-89](), [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:93-126](), [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:129-153]()

## Format-Specific Details

### Amber NetCDF Format

The Amber NetCDF format is a binary format based on the NetCDF (Network Common Data Form) library. It offers several advantages over ASCII formats:

- Binary representation for better precision
- Self-describing format with metadata
- Efficient random access to frames
- Support for additional data (velocities, forces, etc.)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Amber NetCDF Structure"
        Header["Header (Metadata)"]
        Coords["Coordinates (atom×3)"]
        Vels["Velocities (optional)"]
        Forces["Forces (optional)"]
        Box["Unit Cell (optional)"]
        Time["Time (optional)"]
        Temp["Temperature (optional)"]
        REMD["REMD info (optional)"]
    end

    Header --> Coords
    Header --> Vels
    Header --> Forces
    Header --> Box
    Header --> Time
    Header --> Temp
    Header --> REMD
```

#### NetCDF Reading Options
- `usevelascoords`: Use velocities instead of coordinates
- `usefrcascoords`: Use forces instead of coordinates

#### NetCDF Writing Options
- `remdtraj`: Include temperature information (makes a REMD trajectory)
- `mdvel`: Write only velocities to trajectory
- `mdfrc`: Write only forces to trajectory
- `mdcrd`: Write coordinates (only needed when specifying mdvel/mdfrc)
- `hdf5`: Create file as NetCDF4/HDF5 instead of NetCDF3
- `compress`: Use compression in HDF5 file
- `icompress`: Use lossy compression via integer conversion (HDF5 only)

Sources: [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.cpp:72-116](), [src/NetcdfFile.cpp:27-43](), [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.h:13-25]()

### Amber ASCII Trajectory Format

The traditional Amber trajectory format is an ASCII file with coordinates written in a fixed-width format. Each coordinate is written as an 8.3 floating point number, with 10 values per line.

#### ASCII Format Reading
The format is detected by checking if the second line contains atom coordinates in the expected format.

#### ASCII Format Writing Options
- `remdtraj`: Include replica temperature information
- `highprecision`: Use higher precision format (12.7) for writing coordinates
- `mdvel`: Write velocities instead of coordinates
- `mdfrc`: Write forces instead of coordinates

Sources: [src/Traj_AmberCoord.cpp:44-80](), [src/Traj_AmberCoord.h:12-24]()

### Amber Restart Format

Amber restart files contain a snapshot of a simulation:
- Title line
- Number of atoms (and optionally time and temperature) 
- Coordinates for all atoms (formatted as 6 float values per line)
- Optionally velocities (same format as coordinates)
- Optionally box dimensions

#### Restart Format Reading
Restart files are identified by the presence of an integer (atom count) followed by 0-2 scientific floats (time, temperature) and then a line with 3 or more coordinates in the expected format.

#### Restart Format Writing Options
- `remdtraj`: Write temperature to restart file (also writes time)
- `time0`: Time for first frame (if not specified, time is not written)
- `dt`: Time step for subsequent frames, t=(time0+frame)*dt (default: 1.0)
- `keepext`: Keep filename extension; write '<name>.<num>.<ext>' instead

Sources: [src/Traj_AmberRestart.cpp:30-53](), [src/Traj_AmberRestart.cpp:64-79](), [src/Traj_AmberRestart.h:7-19]()

### PDB Format

The PDB (Protein Data Bank) format is a widely used standard for representing molecular structures. CPPTRAJ's implementation supports both reading and writing PDB files.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "PDB File Structure"
        Header["Header Records (TITLE, REMARK, etc.)"]
        SSbonds["SSBOND Records (optional)"]
        Cryst["CRYST1 Record (optional)"]
        Model["MODEL Record (if multiple frames)"]
        Atoms["ATOM/HETATM Records"]
        Ter["TER Records"]
        Conect["CONECT Records (optional)"]
        End["END/ENDMDL Record"]
    end

    Header --> SSbonds
    SSbonds --> Cryst
    Cryst --> Model
    Model --> Atoms
    Atoms --> Ter
    Ter --> Conect
    Conect --> End
```

#### PDB Reading Options
- `keepaltloc <char>`: If specified, alternate location ID to keep

#### PDB Writing Options
- `dumpq`: Write atom charge/GB radius in occupancy/B-factor columns (PQR format)
- `parse`: Write atom charge/PARSE radius in occupancy/B-factor columns (PQR format)
- `vdw`: Write atom charge/VDW radius in occupancy/B-factor columns (PQR format)
- `pdbres`: Use PDB V3 residue names
- `pdbatom`: Use PDB V3 atom names
- `pdbv3`: Use PDB V3 residue/atom names
- `model`: Write to single file separated by MODEL records
- `multi`: Write each frame to separate files
- `conect`: Write CONECT records using bond information

Sources: [src/Traj_PDBfile.cpp:68-265](), [src/PDBfile.cpp:166-256]()

### Charmm DCD Format

The DCD format is a binary trajectory format originally developed for the CHARMM molecular dynamics package.

#### DCD Reading Options
- `shape`: Force reading of box info as CHARMM shape matrix (XX XY YY XZ YZ ZZ)
- `namdcell`: Force reading of box info as NAMD unit cell (X cos(g) Y cos(b) cos(a) Z)
- `charmmcell`: Force reading of box info as old CHARMM unit cell (X Y Z a b g)

The DCD format is detected by checking for 'CORD' or 'VELD' strings in the file header and determining the endianness and bit size.

Sources: [src/Traj_CharmmDcd.cpp:237-254](), [src/Traj_CharmmDcd.cpp:74-118]()

## Reading and Writing Trajectory Data

### Reading Process

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Start Reading"] --> Detect["Detect Format"]
    Detect --> Setup["Setup Trajectory\nsetupTrajin()"]
    Setup --> Open["Open File\nopenTrajin()"]
    Open --> ReadFrame["Read Frame\nreadFrame()"]
    ReadFrame --> Process["Process Frame"]
    Process --> More{{"More Frames?"}}
    More -- "Yes" --> ReadFrame
    More -- "No" --> Close["Close File\ncloseTraj()"]
    Close --> End["End"]
```

Sources: [src/TrajectoryIO.h:34-44]()

### Writing Process

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Start Writing"] --> GetFormat["Get Format from Arguments"]
    GetFormat --> Setup["Setup Trajectory\nsetupTrajout()"]
    Setup --> WriteTitle["Write Title/Header"]
    WriteTitle --> WriteFrame["Write Frame\nwriteFrame()"]
    WriteFrame --> More{{"More Frames?"}}
    More -- "Yes" --> WriteFrame
    More -- "No" --> Close["Close File\ncloseTraj()"]
    Close --> End["End"]
```

Sources: [src/TrajectoryIO.h:46-55]()

## Advanced Features

### Compression Options

Several trajectory formats support compression to reduce file size:

- NetCDF HDF5 offers standard compression with `compress` option
- NetCDF HDF5 supports lossy compression with `icompress` option, which converts coordinates to integers
- Gromacs XTC format uses lossy compression natively

### Parallel I/O

Some trajectory formats support parallel I/O operations in MPI builds:

- NetCDF formats can use parallel NetCDF for efficient parallel reading/writing
- Other formats use serial I/O even in parallel builds

Sources: [src/Traj_AmberNetcdf.cpp:513-516]()

## Format Conversion

CPPTRAJ can be used to convert trajectories between formats. This is done by reading frames from one format and writing them to another. This capability is valuable for:

- Reducing file size (e.g., converting to compressed formats)
- Adding or extracting information (coordinates, velocities, forces)
- Converting between simulation packages
- Creating visualization-friendly formats from simulation outputs

## Format Detection

CPPTRAJ uses a combination of file extension matching and content examination to determine trajectory formats. Each format implementation provides an `ID_TrajFormat` method that examines the file header to determine if it matches that format.

Sources: [src/TrajectoryFile.cpp:158-180]()

# Data File I/O

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/DataFile.cpp](src/DataFile.cpp)
- [src/DataFile.h](src/DataFile.h)
- [src/DataFileList.cpp](src/DataFileList.cpp)

- [src/DataIO.h](src/DataIO.h)
- [src/DataIO_Gnuplot.cpp](src/DataIO_Gnuplot.cpp)
- [src/DataIO_Gnuplot.h](src/DataIO_Gnuplot.h)
- [src/DataIO_Grace.cpp](src/DataIO_Grace.cpp)
- [src/DataIO_Grace.h](src/DataIO_Grace.h)
- [src/DataIO_Mdout.cpp](src/DataIO_Mdout.cpp)
- [src/DataIO_Mdout.h](src/DataIO_Mdout.h)
- [src/DataIO_Std.cpp](src/DataIO_Std.cpp)

- [src/DataSet.h](src/DataSet.h)
- [src/DataSetList.cpp](src/DataSetList.cpp)
- [src/DataSetList.h](src/DataSetList.h)

</details>



This document covers CPPTRAJ's data file input/output system, which is responsible for reading data from files and writing analysis results to files in various formats. For information about trajectory file I/O, see [Trajectory File Formats](#5.1).

## Overview

CPPTRAJ's Data File I/O system provides a flexible framework for reading data from and writing data to files in multiple formats. The system separates the concerns of file management, format-specific I/O operations, and data storage, allowing for easy extension with new file formats.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DataFile {
        -DataSetList SetList_
        -DataIO* dataio_
        -FileName filename_
        +AddDataSet(DataSet*)
        +WriteDataOut()
        +SetupDatafile()
        +ReadDataIn()
    }
    
    class DataFileList {
        -vector fileList_
        -vector cfList_
        +AddDataFile()
        +WriteAllDF()
        +GetDataFile()
    }
    
    class DataIO {
        <<abstract>>
        +ReadData()
        +WriteData()
        +processReadArgs()
        +processWriteArgs()
    }
    
    class DataIO_Std {
        +ReadData()
        +WriteData()
    }
    
    class DataIO_Grace {
        +ReadData()
        +WriteData()
    }
    
    class DataIO_Gnuplot {
        +ReadData()
        +WriteData()
    }
    
    DataFile --> DataIO : uses
    DataFile --> DataSetList : contains
    DataFileList --> DataFile : manages
    DataIO <|-- DataIO_Std : implements
    DataIO <|-- DataIO_Grace : implements
    DataIO <|-- DataIO_Gnuplot : implements
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.h:1-126](). [src/DataFileList.h:1-114](). [src/DataIO.h:1-59]().

## Core Classes

### DataFile

The `DataFile` class represents a data file that can contain multiple `DataSet` objects. It serves as the main interface between the data sets and the file I/O operations. Each `DataFile` instance has:

- A filename (`filename_`)
- A format type (`dfType_`)
- A list of data sets to be written to the file (`SetList_`)
- A `DataIO` object responsible for the actual I/O operations (`dataio_`)

Key responsibilities include:
- Setting up files for reading or writing
- Adding data sets to be written
- Coordinating the reading/writing operations via the `DataIO` object

Sources: [src/DataFile.h:1-126](). [src/DataFile.cpp:1-669]().

### DataFileList

The `DataFileList` class manages a collection of `DataFile` objects. It provides methods for:

- Adding new data files
- Retrieving existing data files
- Writing all data files in the list
- Processing command-line arguments related to data files

This class is useful for directing multiple data sets to the same file and managing file-related options.

Sources: [src/DataFileList.h:1-114](). [src/DataFileList.cpp:1-470]().

### DataIO

`DataIO` is an abstract base class that defines the interface for reading from and writing to specific file formats. The key methods include:

- `ReadData`: Read data from a file into a DataSetList
- `WriteData`: Write data from a DataSetList to a file
- `processReadArgs`: Process format-specific read arguments
- `processWriteArgs`: Process format-specific write arguments

Each specific file format has its own implementation of `DataIO`.

Sources: [src/DataIO.h:1-59](). [src/DataIO.cpp:1-122]().

## Data Flow

The following diagram illustrates the data flow during reading and writing operations:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Read Process"
        R1[User Command] --> R2["DataFile.ReadDataIn()"]
        R2 --> R3["Detect Format"]
        R3 --> R4["Create DataIO"]
        R4 --> R5["DataIO.ReadData()"]
        R5 --> R6["Create DataSets"]
        R6 --> R7["Add to DataSetList"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Write Process"
        W1[User Command] --> W2["DataFileList.WriteAllDF()"]
        W2 --> W3["DataFile.WriteDataOut()"]
        W3 --> W4["DataIO.WriteData()"]
        W4 --> W5["Write Sets to File"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.cpp:178-247](). [src/DataFile.cpp:601-628]().

## Supported File Formats

CPPTRAJ supports numerous file formats for data input and output through various implementations of the `DataIO` interface:

| Format Type | File Extension | DataIO Implementation | Description |
|-------------|----------------|----------------------|-------------|
| Standard    | .dat           | DataIO_Std           | Simple text format with columns of data |
| Grace       | .agr, .xmgr    | DataIO_Grace         | XMGrace plotting program format |
| Gnuplot     | .gnu           | DataIO_Gnuplot       | Gnuplot plotting program format |
| Xplor       | .xplor, .grid  | DataIO_Xplor         | Xplor electron density map format |
| OpenDX      | .dx            | DataIO_OpenDx        | Open Data Explorer format |
| RemLog      | .log           | DataIO_RemLog        | Amber REMD log format |
| Mdout       | .mdout         | DataIO_Mdout         | Amber MD output format |
| Evecs       | .evecs         | DataIO_Evecs         | Eigenvector file format |
| VecTraj     | .vectraj       | DataIO_VecTraj       | Vector pseudo-trajectory format |
| XVG         | .xvg           | DataIO_XVG           | GROMACS graph format |
| CCP4        | .ccp4          | DataIO_CCP4          | CCP4 electron density map format |
| NetCDF      | .nc            | DataIO_NetCDF        | NetCDF format for various data types |

Sources: [src/DataFile.cpp:58-93](). [src/DataFile.cpp:95-122](). [src/DataFile.cpp:124-143]().

## Reading Data

The process of reading data from a file involves several steps:

1. Determining the file format
2. Creating the appropriate `DataIO` object
3. Processing format-specific arguments
4. Reading the data into data sets
5. Adding those data sets to a `DataSetList`

### Format Detection

CPPTRAJ can detect the file format based on the file extension or through explicit specification using the `as` keyword. If the format is not specified and cannot be determined from the extension, CPPTRAJ defaults to the standard format.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["ReadDataIn(filename, args, dsl)"] --> B{"'as' keyword\nin args?"}
    B -->|Yes| C["Get format from\nkeyword"]
    B -->|No| D["DetectFormat(filename)"]
    D -->|Success| E["Return detected\nDataIO"]
    D -->|Failure| F["Get format from\nfile extension"]
    C --> G["Create DataIO\nobject"]
    E --> G
    F --> G
    G --> H["processReadArgs(args)"]
    H --> I["ReadData(filename, dsl, dsname)"]
    I --> J["Return status"]
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.cpp:153-167](). [src/DataFile.cpp:178-248]().

### Example: Reading Standard Format Data

The standard format reader (`DataIO_Std`) is the most versatile and can handle various types of data:

- 1D data (columns of values)
- 2D data (matrices)
- 3D data (volumetric grids)
- Vectors
- 3x3 matrices

When reading 1D data, it automatically determines the type of each column (integer, float, double, string) and creates appropriate data sets.

Sources: [src/DataIO_Std.cpp:102-410](). [src/DataIO_Std.h:16-64]().

## Writing Data

Writing data to files involves:

1. Setting up a `DataFile` with the desired format
2. Adding data sets to the `DataFile`
3. Calling `WriteDataOut()` to write the data sets to the file

### Writing Process Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant DataFileList
    participant DataFile
    participant DataIO
    participant FileSystem
    
    User->>DataFileList: WriteAllDF()
    DataFileList->>DataFile: WriteDataOut() for each file
    alt With ensemble extension
        DataFile->>DataFile: WriteWithEnsExtension()
        DataFile->>DataIO: WriteSetsToFile() for each ensemble
    else Without ensemble extension
        DataFile->>DataFile: WriteNoEnsExtension()
        DataFile->>DataIO: WriteSetsToFile()
    end
    DataIO->>FileSystem: Format-specific write operations
    FileSystem-->>DataIO: Write status
    DataIO-->>DataFile: Return status
    DataFile-->>DataFileList: Return status
    DataFileList-->>User: Complete
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.cpp:525-640](). [src/DataFileList.cpp:358-407]().

### Format-Specific Options

Each file format has its own set of options that can be specified when setting up the `DataFile`. These options are processed by the format-specific `DataIO` implementation.

For example, the standard format (`DataIO_Std`) supports options for:

- Precision (float or double)
- Column labels
- Data grouping

While the Grace format (`DataIO_Grace`) has options for:

- Inverting X/Y axes
- XYDY data format

And the Gnuplot format (`DataIO_Gnuplot`) offers options for:

- PM3D output
- Color palettes
- JPEG output

Sources: [src/DataIO_Std.cpp:76-97](). [src/DataIO_Grace.cpp:121-126](). [src/DataIO_Gnuplot.cpp:218-239]().

## Command Usage Examples

Here are examples of how to use the Data File I/O system from the CPPTRAJ command line:

1. Reading data from a file:
```
readdata data.dat
```

2. Reading with format specification:
```
readdata data.xmgr as grace
```

3. Writing data to a file:
```
writedata output.dat data1,data2,data3
```

4. Writing with format-specific options:
```
writedata output.gnu data1,data2,data3 gnu xpm3d
```

5. Setting precision for output:
```
writedata output.dat data1,data2,data3 prec 10.4
```

Sources: [src/DataFile.cpp:145-151](). [src/DataFile.cpp:443-516]().

## Internal Data Representation

Data read from files is stored in `DataSet` objects, which are organized in a `DataSetList`. The `DataSet` base class has various specialized implementations for different data types:

- `DataSet_double`, `DataSet_float`, `DataSet_integer` for scalar data
- `DataSet_MatrixDbl`, `DataSet_MatrixFlt` for 2D data
- `DataSet_Grid` for 3D data
- `DataSet_Vector` for vector data

Each `DataSet` has associated metadata that describes its dimensions, labels, and other attributes.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DataSet {
        <<abstract>>
        +MetaData meta_
        +TextFormat format_
        +vector dim_
        +Type()
        +Size()
        +Ndim()
    }
    
    class DataSet_1D {
        <<abstract>>
        +Dval(idx)
        +Xval(idx)
    }
    
    class DataSet_2D {
        <<abstract>>
        +GetElement(row, col)
        +SetElement(row, col, value)
    }
    
    class DataSet_3D {
        <<abstract>>
        +GetVoxel(x, y, z)
        +SetVoxel(x, y, z, value)
    }
    
    class DataSet_double {
        +vector Data_
        +AddElement(value)
    }
    
    class DataSet_MatrixDbl {
        +matrix Data_
        +Allocate(rows, cols)
    }
    
    DataSet <|-- DataSet_1D
    DataSet <|-- DataSet_2D
    DataSet <|-- DataSet_3D
    DataSet_1D <|-- DataSet_double
    DataSet_2D <|-- DataSet_MatrixDbl
```

Sources: [src/DataSet.h:1-168](). [src/DataSet.cpp:1-144](). [src/DataSetList.h:1-206](). [src/DataSetList.cpp:1-1666]().

## Extending the System with New Formats

To add support for a new file format, you would need to:

1. Create a new class deriving from `DataIO`
2. Implement the required methods:
   - `ReadData`
   - `WriteData`
   - `processReadArgs`
   - `processWriteArgs`
   - `ID_DataFormat`
3. Register the new format in the `DataFile` static arrays:
   - `DF_AllocArray`
   - `DF_KeyArray`
   - `DF_WriteKeyArray`

This modular design makes it straightforward to extend the system with new file formats without modifying the core data management classes.

Sources: [src/DataFile.cpp:58-93](). [src/DataFile.cpp:95-122](). [src/DataFile.cpp:124-143]().

This page documents the analysis capabilities in CPPTRAJ, which allow users to analyze data generated from trajectory processing or external sources. CPPTRAJ provides a rich set of analysis methods ranging from statistical analysis to advanced molecular structure characterization. For information about trajectory processing actions, see [Core Architecture](#3).

## Analysis Framework Overview

CPPTRAJ divides analysis capabilities into two primary categories:

1. **Actions** - Operations performed on coordinate frames as they are read during trajectory processing
2. **Analyses** - Operations performed on accumulated data after frames have been processed

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Analysis Categories"
        Actions["Actions"]
        Analyses["Analyses"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Action Categories"
        Transformations["Coordinate Transformations"]
        PropertyCalc["Property Calculations"]
        StructAnalysis["Structural Analysis"]
        EnergyCalc["Energy Calculations"]
        NAAnalysis["Nucleic Acid Analysis"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis Categories"
        Clustering["Clustering"]
        Statistics["Statistical Analysis"]
        Correlation["Correlation Analysis"]
        GIST["Grid Inhomogeneous Solvation Theory"]
    end
    
    Actions --> Transformations
    Actions --> PropertyCalc
    Actions --> StructAnalysis
    Actions --> EnergyCalc
    Actions --> NAAnalysis
    
    Analyses --> Clustering
    Analyses --> Statistics
    Analyses --> Correlation
    Analyses --> GIST
```

Sources: [src/Command.cpp:74-169](). [src/Command.cpp:170-215]().

## Analysis Execution Flow

Analysis operations in CPPTRAJ follow a specific execution flow:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Command
    participant CpptrajState
    participant AnalysisList
    participant Analysis
    
    User->>Command: Input analysis command
    Command->>CpptrajState: AddToAnalysisQueue()
    CpptrajState->>AnalysisList: AddAnalysis()
    
    Note over User,Analysis: After trajectory processing complete
    
    User->>Command: run/go command
    Command->>CpptrajState: Run()
    CpptrajState->>AnalysisList: DoAnalyses()
    AnalysisList->>Analysis: Setup()
    AnalysisList->>Analysis: Analyze()
    Analysis-->>User: Output results
```

Sources: [src/Command.cpp:604-662]().

## Key Analysis Features

### Clustering

Clustering groups similar conformations together based on a distance metric, useful for identifying dominant states in a simulation.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Data["DataSets or Coordinates"] --> Clustering["Clustering Algorithms"]
    Clustering --> |"Process"|ClusterResults["Cluster Results"]
    
    subgraph "ClusterMethods"
        Hierarchical["Hierarchical"]
        KMeans["K-Means"]
        DBSCAN["DBSCAN"]
    end
    
    subgraph "DistanceMethods"
        RMSD["RMSD"]
        DME["Distance RMSD"]
        DSR["Dataset RMSD"]
    end
    
    Clustering --- ClusterMethods
    Clustering --- DistanceMethods
    
    ClusterResults --> |"Generate"|Representatives["Representative Structures"]
    ClusterResults --> |"Calculate"|ClusterStats["Cluster Statistics"]
```

CPPTRAJ provides multiple clustering algorithms:
- Hierarchical (bottom-up, top-down)
- K-means
- DBSCAN
- DPeaks (density peaks)

Distance metrics include:
- RMSD (standard, best-fit, mass-weighted, symmetry-corrected)
- Distance-RMSD
- Dataset-based metrics

Sources: [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:1-75](). [test/Makefile:102-116]().

### Nucleic Acid Structure Analysis (NAstruct)

NAstruct calculates structural parameters for nucleic acids following established conventions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Coordinates --> |"Process"|NAstruct["NA Structure Analysis"]
    
    NAstruct --> BasePairs["Base Pair Parameters"]
    NAstruct --> BaseSteps["Base Pair Step Parameters"]
    NAstruct --> HelicalParams["Helical Parameters"]
    
    subgraph "Base Pair Parameters"
        Shear["Shear"]
        Stretch["Stretch"]
        Stagger["Stagger"]
        Buckle["Buckle"]
        Propeller["Propeller Twist"]
        Opening["Opening"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Base Pair Step Parameters"
        Shift["Shift"]
        Slide["Slide"]
        Rise["Rise"]
        Tilt["Tilt"]
        Roll["Roll"]
        Twist["Twist"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Helical Parameters"
        XDisp["X-displacement"]
        YDisp["Y-displacement"]
        HRise["Helical Rise"]
        Inclination["Inclination"]
        TipAngle["Tip Angle"]
        HTwist["Helical Twist"]
    end
```

Features of NAstruct:
- Compatible with standard 3DNA and Curves+ conventions
- Support for custom base pair definitions
- Multiple options for determining base pairing
- Groove width calculations
- Analysis of non-canonical structures
- Output of base reference frames

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:1-454](). [src/Action_NAstruct.h:1-139](). [src/AxisType.cpp:1-66](). [test/Makefile:70-72]().

### Energy Calculations

CPPTRAJ can calculate various energy terms for molecules or systems.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Coordinates --> |"Process"|Energy["Energy Calculation"]
    
    Energy --> BondedEnergy["Bonded Energy Terms"]
    Energy --> NonbondedEnergy["Non-bonded Energy Terms"]
    
    subgraph "Bonded Terms"
        Bond["Bond Energy"]
        Angle["Angle Energy"]
        Dihedral["Dihedral Energy"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Non-bonded Terms"
        VDW["Van der Waals"]
        Electrostatic["Electrostatic"]
        subgraph "Electrostatic Methods"
            Simple["Simple Cutoff"]
            DirectSum["Direct Sum"]
            PME["Particle Mesh Ewald"]
        end
    end
    
    BondedEnergy --- Bond
    BondedEnergy --- Angle
    BondedEnergy --- Dihedral
    NonbondedEnergy --- VDW
    NonbondedEnergy --- Electrostatic
    Electrostatic --- ElectrostaticMethods
```

Energy calculation features:
- Multiple supported terms (bond, angle, dihedral, non-bonded)
- Various electrostatic calculation methods (simple, direct sum, Ewald, PME)
- OpenMM integration for full potential calculations
- Support for kinetic energy calculations
- Per-residue and per-molecule decomposition

Sources: [src/Action_Energy.cpp:1-100](). [src/Action_Energy.h:1-30](). [src/Energy.cpp:1-56](). [test/Makefile:278-280]().

### Grid Inhomogeneous Solvation Theory (GIST)

GIST is a method for analyzing the thermodynamic properties of water molecules on a 3D grid.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Trajectory --> |"Process"|GIST["GIST Analysis"]
    
    GIST --> GridSetup["3D Grid Setup"]
    GridSetup --> EnergyCalc["Energy Calculations"]
    GridSetup --> EntropyCalc["Entropy Calculations"]
    GridSetup --> DensityCalc["Density Calculations"]
    
    EnergyCalc --> |"Calculate"|EswMap["Water-Solute Energy Map"]
    EnergyCalc --> |"Calculate"|EwwMap["Water-Water Energy Map"]
    
    EntropyCalc --> |"Calculate"|TransEntropy["Translational Entropy"]
    EntropyCalc --> |"Calculate"|OrientEntropy["Orientational Entropy"]
    
    DensityCalc --> |"Calculate"|WaterDensity["Water Density Map"]
    
    subgraph "Output"
        DXFiles["DX Grid Files"]
        DataFile["Summary Data File"]
    end
    
    EswMap --> DXFiles
    EwwMap --> DXFiles
    TransEntropy --> DXFiles
    OrientEntropy --> DXFiles
    WaterDensity --> DXFiles
    
    GIST --> DataFile
```

GIST analysis features:
- 3D grid-based analysis of solvent properties
- Water-water and water-solute interaction energies
- Translational and orientational entropy calculations
- Order parameter calculations
- Support for PME-based energy calculations
- CUDA acceleration for performance
- Output in standard visualizable formats

Sources: [src/Action_GIST.cpp:1-321](). [src/Action_GIST.h:1-136](). [test/Test_GIST/RunTest.sh:1-11](). [test/Makefile:205-207]().

## Statistical Analyses

CPPTRAJ includes numerous statistical analysis tools for processing trajectory-derived data:

| Analysis Type | Description | Key Features |
|--------------|-------------|--------------|
| Correlation | Calculate auto/cross-correlation between time series | Supports FFT methods, handles multiple datasets |
| Regression | Linear/polynomial regression analysis | Supports weighted fits, multiple datasets |
| Clustering | Group similar conformations | Multiple algorithms and metrics |
| Histogram | Generate 1D/2D histograms of data | Customizable bin sizes, normalization |
| Wavelet | Time-frequency analysis | Multi-resolution capabilities |
| IRED | Isotropic Reorientational Eigenmode Dynamics | Model-free approach for NMR order parameters |
| Lifetime | Analyze state transitions | Statistics on persistence of interactions |
| Timeseries | Time series analysis tools | Autocorrelation, moving averages |

Sources: [src/Command.cpp:171-214](). [test/Makefile:89-116](). [test/Makefile:117-145]().

## Data Management for Analysis

Analysis features in CPPTRAJ rely on a sophisticated data management system:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Data Production"
        Actions["Actions"]
        InputData["External Data Sources"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Storage"
        DataSetList["DataSetList"]
        DataSets["DataSets"]
        DataFile["DataFile"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis"
        AnalysisList["AnalysisList"]
        AnalysisModules["Analysis Modules"]
    end
    
    Actions --> |"Generate"|DataSets
    InputData --> |"Load"|DataSets
    DataSets --> |"Stored in"|DataSetList
    DataSets --> |"Written to"|DataFile
    DataSetList --> |"Input for"|AnalysisModules
    AnalysisModules --> |"Managed by"|AnalysisList
    AnalysisModules --> |"Generate"|DataSets
```

Key aspects of the data management system:
- Various dataset types (scalars, vectors, matrices, grids)
- Flexible data access and manipulation
- Unified interface for file I/O
- Support for mathematical operations on datasets
- Integration between Actions and Analyses

Sources: [src/Command.cpp:227-245](). [test/Makefile:209-210](). [test/Makefile:337-339]().

## Implementing Custom Analysis

CPPTRAJ has an extensible architecture that allows new analysis methods to be added:

1. For new **Actions**, create a class that inherits from `Action` with the required methods:
   - `Init()` - Initialize the action with command line arguments
   - `Setup()` - Set up the action for a specific topology
   - `DoAction()` - Process each frame
   - `Print()` - Output results

2. For new **Analyses**, create a class that inherits from `Analysis` with the required methods:
   - `Setup()` - Initialize the analysis with command line arguments
   - `Analyze()` - Perform the analysis on accumulated data

3. Register the new analysis in `Command.cpp` using `Command::AddCmd()` to make it available to users

Sources: [src/Command.cpp:226-478](). [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:1-75](). [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:1-139]().

## Parallel Analysis

Many CPPTRAJ analysis methods support parallel processing through OpenMP and MPI:

- **OpenMP** parallelization for shared-memory performance on multi-core systems
- **MPI** parallelization for distributed-memory systems and cluster computing
- Support for ensemble-level parallelism (multiple trajectories)
- Frame-level parallelism for certain compute-intensive analyses

Sources: [src/Action_GIST.cpp:14-16](). [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:43-47]().

## Analysis Data Visualization

Analysis results can be output in various formats for visualization:

- Standard data file formats (text, CSV, etc.)
- Grace/xmgrace format for 2D plotting
- DX format for 3D grid visualization
- PDB/trajectory files for structural outputs
- NumPy-compatible formats for integration with Python tools

Sources: [test/Test_GIST/RunTest.sh:5-10](). [test/Test_ReadData/RunTest.sh:5-7]().

# Page: Clustering

# Clustering

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp](src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp)
- [src/Analysis_Clustering.h](src/Analysis_Clustering.h)

</details>



This document provides a comprehensive overview of the clustering functionality in CPPTRAJ. Clustering is a powerful analysis technique that groups similar conformations from molecular dynamics trajectories, helping researchers identify predominant structural states and simplify trajectory analysis. For other analysis features, see [Analysis Features](#6).

## Purpose and Overview

Clustering in CPPTRAJ allows users to group trajectory frames based on structural similarity or other metrics. The implementation supports multiple clustering algorithms, distance metrics, and processing options to accommodate different research needs. This system enables:

- Identification of representative structures from large trajectory datasets
- Analysis of conformational space sampling
- Reduction of trajectory complexity for further analysis
- Generation of structural ensembles for visualization and interpretation

Sources: [src/Analysis_Clustering.h:5-6]()

## Integration with CPPTRAJ Architecture

Clustering is implemented as an Analysis module within CPPTRAJ's Analysis Engine. It operates on trajectory data or other datasets and produces clustered datasets that can be further processed or output.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "CPPTRAJ Analysis Engine"
        Analysis["Analysis Base Class"]
        Actions["Actions"]
        Analyses["Analyses"]
        
        Analysis --> Actions
        Analysis --> Analyses
        
        subgraph "Analysis Implementations"
            Clustering["Analysis_Clustering"]
            Statistics["Statistical Analysis"]
            Correlation["Correlation Analysis"]
            GIST["Grid-Based Analysis"]
        end
        
        Analyses --> Clustering
        Analyses --> Statistics
        Analyses --> Correlation
        Analyses --> GIST
    end
    
    subgraph "Clustering Components"
        ClusterControl["Cluster::Control"]
        Algorithms["Clustering Algorithms"]
        Metrics["Distance Metrics"]
        Output["Output Generation"]
        
        ClusterControl --> Algorithms
        ClusterControl --> Metrics
        ClusterControl --> Output
    end
    
    Clustering --> ClusterControl
```

Sources: [src/Analysis_Clustering.h:1-19](), [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:4-5]()

## Class Structure

The clustering functionality is primarily implemented through two key classes:

1. `Analysis_Clustering` - Entry point that inherits from the `Analysis` base class
2. `Cpptraj::Cluster::Control` - Core implementation that handles the clustering algorithms and processing

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Analysis {
        <<abstract>>
        +Setup(ArgList&, AnalysisSetup&, int)
        +Analyze()
        +Help()
    }
    
    class Analysis_Clustering {
        -Cpptraj::Cluster::Control control_
        -DataSetList* masterDSL_
        +Setup(ArgList&, AnalysisSetup&, int)
        +Analyze()
        +Help()
    }
    
    class Control {
        +SetupClustering()
        +Run()
        +Output()
        +Timing()
        +Info()
        +Help()
    }
    
    Analysis <|-- Analysis_Clustering : inherits
    Analysis_Clustering *-- "1" Control : contains
    Analysis_Clustering --> DataSetList : references
```

Sources: [src/Analysis_Clustering.h:4-18](), [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:4-15]()

## Processing Workflow

The clustering analysis follows a specific workflow through the CPPTRAJ processing pipeline:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Analysis_Clustering
    participant Control
    participant DataSets
    
    User->>Analysis_Clustering: Setup with arguments
    Analysis_Clustering->>DataSets: Get input data sets
    DataSets-->>Analysis_Clustering: Return coordinates or metrics
    Analysis_Clustering->>Control: SetupClustering(inputDsets, coords, args)
    Control-->>Analysis_Clustering: Setup complete
    
    User->>Analysis_Clustering: Analyze()
    Analysis_Clustering->>Control: Run()
    Control->>Control: Perform clustering algorithm
    Control-->>Analysis_Clustering: Clustering complete
    Analysis_Clustering->>Control: Output(*masterDSL_)
    Control->>DataSets: Add cluster results
    Control-->>Analysis_Clustering: Output complete
    Analysis_Clustering-->>User: Analysis results
```

Sources: [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:14-75]()

## Data Handling

Clustering can be performed on two types of input data:

1. **Coordinate Data** (`DataSet_Coords`): Clustering based on structural similarity of trajectory frames
2. **Generic Data Sets**: Clustering based on arbitrary data metrics

The input data selection is handled in the `Setup()` method of `Analysis_Clustering`:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Setup()"] --> CheckData["Check for 'data' key"]
    
    CheckData -->|"data specified"| GetDataSets["Get multiple data sets"]
    GetDataSets --> CheckCoords["Check for 'crdset' or !nocoords"]
    
    CheckData -->|"data not specified"| CheckCoords
    
    CheckCoords -->|"coords needed"| FindCoords["Find COORDS dataset"]
    FindCoords -->|"no data specified"| AddCoords["Add coordinates to input datasets"]
    FindCoords --> SetupCluster["control_.SetupClustering()"]
    
    CheckCoords -->|"coords not needed"| SetupCluster
    
    SetupCluster --> Info["control_.Info()"]
    Info --> End["Return"]
```

Sources: [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:14-56]()

## Clustering Execution

The actual clustering analysis is executed in the `Analyze()` method:

1. Start a timer to measure performance
2. Call `control_.Run()` to execute the clustering algorithm
3. Call `control_.Output(*masterDSL_)` to generate output data
4. Stop the timer and record timing information

Sources: [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:59-75]()

## Supported Clustering Algorithms

CPPTRAJ supports multiple clustering algorithms, including:

| Algorithm | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Hierarchical | Groups data points based on distance between them in a tree-like structure |
| K-means | Partitions data into k clusters based on the mean distance to cluster centers |
| DBSCAN | Density-based spatial clustering - groups based on regions of high density |
| DPeaks | Density peaks clustering algorithm |

The specific algorithm used is determined by parameters passed during setup.

Sources: System Architecture Diagrams

## Usage Parameters

The clustering functionality accepts several key parameters:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `crdset <crd set>` | Specifies a coordinate dataset for structural clustering |
| `data <dset0>[,<dset1>...]` | Specifies arbitrary datasets for metric-based clustering |
| `nocoords` | Disables use of coordinate data, even if available |

Additional parameters for specific algorithms, distance metrics, and output options are handled by the `Control` class.

Sources: [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:8-11](), [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:19-46]()

## Practical Workflow

The typical workflow for using clustering in CPPTRAJ involves:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    LoadData["Load trajectory\nand topology"] --> SetupClustering["Setup clustering\nparameters"]
    SetupClustering --> RunClustering["Run clustering\nanalysis"]
    RunClustering --> AnalyzeResults["Analyze cluster\nstatistics"]
    AnalyzeResults --> ViewRepresentatives["View representative\nstructures"]
```

## Implementation Notes

1. The `Analysis_Clustering` class acts primarily as a wrapper that delegates the actual clustering functionality to the `Cpptraj::Cluster::Control` class.

2. Input data processing is flexible, allowing for:
   - Coordinate-based clustering (structural similarity)
   - Data metric-based clustering (arbitrary metrics)
   - Combinations of both approaches

3. Performance timing is built in to track the efficiency of the clustering operation.

4. Results are stored in the master DataSetList for further processing or output.

Sources: [src/Analysis_Clustering.cpp:1-76](), [src/Analysis_Clustering.h:1-19]()

## Integration with Other CPPTRAJ Components

Clustering analysis interacts with several other components of CPPTRAJ:

1. **Data Management System**: Results are stored as DataSets
2. **Output System**: Cluster statistics and representative structures can be written to various output formats
3. **Command Processing**: Clustering parameters are parsed from user input

For more information on these related systems, see [Data Management](#4.3) and [Command Processing](#3.1).

---

# Page: Energy Calculations

# Energy Calculations

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/Action_Energy.cpp](src/Action_Energy.cpp)
- [src/Action_Energy.h](src/Action_Energy.h)
- [src/Energy.cpp](src/Energy.cpp)
- [src/Energy.h](src/Energy.h)
- [src/Energy/Ene_Angle.h](src/Energy/Ene_Angle.h)
- [src/PairList.cpp](src/PairList.cpp)
- [src/PairList.h](src/PairList.h)

</details>



This page documents the energy calculation functionality in CPPTRAJ, which provides methods for computing various energy components from molecular simulations. Energy calculations in CPPTRAJ can analyze bond, angle, dihedral, van der Waals, electrostatic, and kinetic energy terms both individually and in combination.

For information about potential functions used by other components, see the Analysis Engine Architecture [Analysis Engine](#6).

## Architecture Overview

Energy calculations in CPPTRAJ are implemented through the Action framework as `Action_Energy`, which uses the `Energy_Amber` class to perform actual calculations. The relationship between these components is illustrated below:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Action_Energy {
        -Energy_Amber ENE_
        -ExclusionArray Excluded_
        -Ecalc_Nonbond NB_
        -CharMask Mask1_
        -AtomMask Imask_
        +Init()
        +Setup()
        +DoAction()
    }
    
    class Energy_Amber {
        +E_bond()
        +E_angle()
        +E_torsion()
        +E_14_Nonbond()
        +E_Nonbond()
        +E_VDW()
        +E_Elec()
        +E_DirectSum()
        +E_Kinetic()
        +E_Kinetic_VV()
    }
    
    class Ecalc_Nonbond {
        +NonbondEnergy()
    }
    
    class PairList {
        +Cell
        +InitPairList()
        +SetupPairList()
        +CreatePairList()
    }
    
    Action_Energy --> Energy_Amber : uses
    Action_Energy --> Ecalc_Nonbond : uses for Ewald/PME
    Ecalc_Nonbond --> PairList : uses for efficiency
```

Sources: [src/Action_Energy.h:10-71](), [src/Energy.h:10-42](), [src/PairList.h:57-173]()

## Energy Components

CPPTRAJ can calculate the following energy components:

| Component | Description | Implementation |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| Bond      | Energy from bond stretching | `E_bond()` |
| Angle     | Energy from angle bending | `E_angle()` |
| Dihedral  | Energy from dihedral torsions | `E_torsion()` |
| VDW       | Van der Waals non-bonded energy | `E_VDW()` |
| Electrostatic | Coulombic interactions | `E_Elec()`, `E_DirectSum()` |
| 1-4 Non-bonded | Scaled interactions between atoms separated by 3 bonds | `E_14_Nonbond()` |
| Kinetic   | Kinetic energy from velocities | `E_Kinetic()`, `E_Kinetic_VV()` |

Sources: [src/Action_Energy.cpp:64-69](), [src/Action_Energy.h:26](), [src/Energy.h:15-27]()

### Calculation Flow

The energy calculation workflow follows this sequence:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Action_Energy::DoAction()"] --> |"For each calculation type"| B["Select calculation"]
    
    B --> C1["Bond Energy"]
    B --> C2["Angle Energy"]
    B --> C3["Dihedral Energy"]
    B --> C4["1-4 Non-bonded"]
    B --> C5["Non-bonded Energy"]
    B --> C6["Kinetic Energy"]
    
    C1 --> D["ENE_.E_bond()"]
    C2 --> E["ENE_.E_angle()"]
    C3 --> F["ENE_.E_torsion()"]
    C4 --> G["ENE_.E_14_Nonbond()"]
    C5 --> H1["ENE_.E_Nonbond()"]
    C5 --> H2["ENE_.E_VDW()"]
    C5 --> H3["ENE_.E_Elec()"]
    C5 --> H4["ENE_.E_DirectSum()"]
    C5 --> H5["NB_.NonbondEnergy()"]
    C6 --> I1["ENE_.E_Kinetic()"]
    C6 --> I2["ENE_.E_Kinetic_VV()"]
    
    H1 --> J["Store results in DataSets"]
    H2 --> J
    H3 --> J
    H4 --> J
    H5 --> J
    D --> J
    E --> J
    F --> J
    G --> J
    I1 --> J
    I2 --> J
```

Sources: [src/Action_Energy.cpp:407-523]()

## Bonded Energy Terms

Bonded energy terms include bond, angle, and dihedral energies which are calculated using the standard Amber force field formulations.

### Bond Energy

Bond energy is calculated using a harmonic potential:

```
E_bond = k * (r - r_eq)²
```

where `k` is the force constant, `r` is the actual bond length, and `r_eq` is the equilibrium bond length.

Implementation uses the `Ene_Bond` templated function to calculate each bond's energy contribution, separately handling bonds to hydrogen if requested.

Sources: [src/Energy.cpp:18-55]()

### Angle Energy

Angle energy uses a harmonic potential around the equilibrium angle:

```
E_angle = k * (θ - θ_eq)²
```

where `θ` is the angle between three atoms and `θ_eq` is the equilibrium angle.

The implementation calculates angles using the dot product of the two bond vectors, ensuring the cosine value stays within reasonable bounds (-0.999 to 0.999).

Sources: [src/Energy.cpp:59-97](), [src/Energy/Ene_Angle.h:6-40]()

### Dihedral Energy

Dihedral energy is calculated using a periodic function:

```
E_dihedral = k * (1 + cos(n*φ - φ_0))
```

where `k` is the force constant, `n` is the periodicity, `φ` is the dihedral angle, and `φ_0` is the phase.

Sources: [src/Energy.cpp:100-142]()

## Non-bonded Energy Terms

Non-bonded energy terms include van der Waals and electrostatic interactions between atoms that are not connected by bonds.

### Van der Waals Energy

Van der Waals energy uses the Lennard-Jones 6-12 potential:

```
E_vdw = (A/r¹²) - (B/r⁶)
```

where `A` and `B` are parameters derived from the atom types, and `r` is the distance between atoms.

Sources: [src/Energy.cpp:268-317]()

### Electrostatics 

Electrostatic energy can be calculated using several methods:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Electrostatic Methods"] --> B["Simple Cutoff"]
    A --> C["Direct Sum"]
    A --> D["Regular Ewald"]
    A --> E["Particle Mesh Ewald (PME)"]
    
    B --> B1["E_Elec()"]
    C --> C1["E_DirectSum()"]
    D --> D1["NB_.NonbondEnergy() with REGULAR_EWALD"]
    E --> E1["NB_.NonbondEnergy() with PME"]
    
    subgraph "Simple Methods"
        B1
        C1
    end
    
    subgraph "Ewald Methods"
        D1
        E1
    end
```

Sources: [src/Action_Energy.cpp:160-196](), [src/Energy.cpp:320-409]()

#### Simple Cutoff Method

The simplest method which calculates Coulomb's law directly:

```
E_elec = q₁q₂/(ε*r)
```

where `q₁` and `q₂` are the charges on the atoms, `ε` is the dielectric constant, and `r` is the distance.

Sources: [src/Energy.cpp:320-365]()

#### Direct Sum Method

Calculates electrostatic energy including periodic images:

```
E_direct = E_elec + ∑(image cells) q₁q₂/(ε*r_image)
```

This method can be computationally expensive for large systems but is useful for validation.

Sources: [src/Energy.cpp:367-409](), [src/Action_Energy.cpp:391-404]()

#### Ewald and PME Methods

For more efficient treatment of long-range electrostatics, CPPTRAJ implements:

1. Regular Ewald Summation - Splits the calculation into short-range and long-range components
2. Particle Mesh Ewald (PME) - Uses Fast Fourier Transforms to accelerate the long-range part

These methods require the `Ecalc_Nonbond` class which uses a spatial grid via `PairList` for efficient calculation.

Sources: [src/Action_Energy.cpp:163-186]()

### 1-4 Non-bonded Interactions

1-4 interactions (between atoms separated by exactly three bonds) are calculated separately with scaling factors (SCNB for VDW, SCEE for electrostatics) to prevent over-estimation of these forces:

```
E_vdw14 = ((A/r¹²) - (B/r⁶)) / SCNB
E_elec14 = (q₁q₂/(ε*r)) / SCEE
```

Sources: [src/Energy.cpp:146-202]()

## Kinetic Energy

CPPTRAJ can calculate kinetic energy in two ways:

1. From velocities directly (on-step): `E_k = 0.5 * m * v²`
2. Using the velocity Verlet approach (half-step velocities): Estimates on-step velocities using force information

Sources: [src/Energy.cpp:412-469](), [src/Action_Energy.cpp:140-156]()

## Efficiency Considerations

### Exclusion Lists

Non-bonded interactions are not calculated between atoms that are already connected via bonds, angles, or dihedrals. CPPTRAJ uses an `ExclusionArray` to track these relationships and skip unnecessary calculations.

Sources: [src/Action_Energy.cpp:345-362]()

### Spatial Decomposition with PairList

For efficient handling of non-bonded interactions, CPPTRAJ implements a grid-based neighbor list through the `PairList` class. This divides the simulation box into grid cells and only calculates interactions between atoms in neighboring cells.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["PairList Setup"] --> B["Divide box into grid cells"]
    B --> C["Determine cell connectivity"]
    C --> D["Assign atoms to cells"]
    D --> E["Calculate interactions only between\nneighboring cells"]
    
    subgraph "Grid-based Approach"
        F["Cell 1"] --- G["Cell 2"]
        F --- H["Cell 3"]
        G --- H
        F --- I["Cell 4"]
        G --- I
        H --- I
    end
```

Sources: [src/PairList.cpp:70-96](), [src/PairList.cpp:159-229]()

## Command Usage

Energy calculations are invoked using the `energy` command in CPPTRAJ:

```
energy [<name>] [<mask1>] [out <filename>] [nobondstoh] [openmm [<mdopts>]]
       [bond] [angle] [dihedral] {[nb14]|[e14]|[v14]} {[nonbond] | [elec] [vdw]}
       [{nokinetic|kinetic [ketype {vel|vv}] [dt <dt>]}]
       [ etype { simple |
                 directsum [npoints <N>] |
                 ewald ... |
                 pme ...
               } ]
```

Key options:
- Specify energy terms to calculate: `bond`, `angle`, `dihedral`, `nonbond`, etc.
- Select electrostatics method: `etype simple|directsum|ewald|pme`
- Kinetic energy options: `kinetic [ketype {vel|vv}] [dt <dt>]`

Sources: [src/Action_Energy.cpp:29-53](), [src/Action_Energy.cpp:86-317]()

## Example Applications

Energy calculations in CPPTRAJ can be used for:

1. Evaluating structure quality by examining energy components
2. Analyzing energy conservation in MD trajectories
3. Comparing different force field terms and their contributions
4. Calculating binding energies by selecting specific groups of atoms

When calculating total energies, it's important to consider which electrostatic method is most appropriate for the system size and boundary conditions.

Sources: [src/Action_Energy.cpp:282-317]()

---

# Page: Nucleic Acid Analysis

# Nucleic Acid Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp](src/Action_NAstruct.cpp)
- [src/Action_NAstruct.h](src/Action_NAstruct.h)
- [src/AxisType.cpp](src/AxisType.cpp)
- [src/AxisType.h](src/AxisType.h)
- [test/Test_NAstruct/RunTest.sh](test/Test_NAstruct/RunTest.sh)
- [test/Test_NAstruct/SS.mol1.dat.save](test/Test_NAstruct/SS.mol1.dat.save)
- [test/Test_NAstruct/SS.mol1.selected.dat.save](test/Test_NAstruct/SS.mol1.selected.dat.save)
- [test/Test_NAstruct/axes.bases.pdb.save](test/Test_NAstruct/axes.bases.pdb.save)
- [test/Test_NAstruct/axes.bp.mol2.save](test/Test_NAstruct/axes.bp.mol2.save)
- [test/Test_NAstruct/axes.step.crd.save](test/Test_NAstruct/axes.step.crd.save)
- [test/Test_NAstruct/axes.step.parm7.save](test/Test_NAstruct/axes.step.parm7.save)

</details>



The Nucleic Acid Analysis module in CPPTRAJ provides comprehensive analysis of nucleic acid structure from molecular dynamics trajectories. It calculates a wide range of geometric parameters describing the spatial arrangements of nucleic acid bases, base pairs, base-pair steps, and helical conformations, allowing detailed characterization of DNA and RNA structural dynamics.

## Overview of NAstruct

The `NAstruct` command enables analysis of nucleic acid structures through several key capabilities:

- Base pair identification through geometric criteria or user specification
- Calculation of standard base-pair parameters (shear, stretch, stagger, buckle, propeller, opening)
- Base-pair step parameters calculation (shift, slide, rise, tilt, roll, twist)
- Helical parameter analysis (x-displacement, y-displacement, inclination, tip)
- Sugar pucker analysis using Altona-Sundaralingam or Cremer-Pople methods
- Groove width measurements
- Single-strand analysis
- Reference frame extraction and visualization

The implementation follows established conventions from structural biology literature, particularly the mathematical framework of Babcock et al. and the standard reference frame definitions of Olson et al.

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.h:12-31](), [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:123-166]()

## System Architecture

### Class Hierarchy

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Action {
        <<abstract>>
        +Init()
        +Setup()
        +DoAction()
    }
    
    class Action_NAstruct {
        -FindType findBPmode_
        -GrooveType grooveCalcType_
        -BP_ConventionType bpConvention_
        -NA_Reference refBases_
        -std::vector~NA_Base~ Bases_
        -BPmap BasePairs_
        -StepMap Steps_
        +Init()
        +Setup()
        +DoAction()
        +SetupBaseAxes()
        +DetermineBasePairing()
        +SpecifiedBasePairing()
        +CalcNumHB()
    }
    
    class NA_Base {
        -NAType type_
        -Frame Ref_
        -Frame Inp_
        -NA_Axis axis_
        -DataSet_1D* pucker_
        +Setup_Base()
        +CalcPucker()
        +SetInputFrame()
    }
    
    class NA_Axis {
        -Matrix_3x3 R_
        -Vec3 origin_
        -Vec3 RX_
        -Vec3 RY_
        -Vec3 RZ_
        +StoreRotMatrix()
        +FlipYZ()
        +FlipXY()
        +FlipXZ()
    }
    
    class NA_Reference {
        -BaseArray bases_
        +SetupBaseRef()
        +AddCustomBase()
        +LoadFromFile()
    }
    
    class RefBase {
        -NA_Array atoms_
        -NameArray names_
        -char baseChar_
        -NAType type_
        +AddName()
        +AddAtom()
        +NameMatches()
    }
    
    class NA_Atom {
        -double x_, y_, z_
        -HBType hb_type_
        -int rms_fit_
        -NameType aname_
    }
    
    Action <|-- Action_NAstruct
    Action_NAstruct o-- NA_Reference
    Action_NAstruct o-- NA_Base
    NA_Base o-- NA_Axis
    NA_Reference o-- RefBase
    RefBase o-- NA_Atom
```

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.h:32-236](), [src/AxisType.h:1-190]()

### Data Structures

The NAstruct implementation uses several specialized data structures to track nucleic acid components and their parameters:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Action_NAstruct {

        -StepType Steps_
        -Stype StrandPairs_
    }

    Action_NAstruct o-- BPtype

```

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.h:56-122]()

## Nucleic Acid Reference Frames

A core concept in nucleic acid analysis is the reference frame assigned to each base. These reference frames enable the calculation of geometric parameters between bases.

### Base Reference Frames

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Base Reference"
        Origin["Origin (C1')"]
        XAxis["X-Axis (Major Groove)"]
        YAxis["Y-Axis (Base/Base-pair Plane)"]
        ZAxis["Z-Axis (Perpendicular to Base)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Base Setup Process"
        InputCoords["Input Coordinates"]
        RefCoords["Reference Coordinates"]
        RMSFit["RMS Fitting"]
        RefFrame["Establish Reference Frame"]
    end
    
    InputCoords --> RMSFit
    RefCoords --> RMSFit
    RMSFit --> RefFrame
    RefFrame --> Origin
    RefFrame --> XAxis
    RefFrame --> YAxis
    RefFrame --> ZAxis
```

Each nucleic acid base is assigned a reference coordinate system following conventions established by Olson et al. The origin is typically placed at the C1' atom, with the axes oriented so that:
- The x-axis points toward the major groove
- The y-axis lies in the base plane
- The z-axis is perpendicular to the base plane

This reference frame is established by fitting standard reference coordinates onto the actual base coordinates from the trajectory.

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:505-581](), [src/AxisType.cpp:40-111]()

## Base Pairing and Parameter Calculation

### Base Pair Determination

CPPTRAJ offers several methods to determine which bases are paired:

1. **First frame** (default): Base pairs are determined from the first trajectory frame and used for all subsequent frames
2. **Reference structure**: Uses a reference structure to define base pairs
3. **All frames**: Base pairs are determined independently for each frame
4. **User-specified**: Base pairs are explicitly defined by the user

Geometric criteria for automatic base pairing include:
- Distance between reference frame origins
- Angle between z-axes
- Presence of hydrogen bonds
- Vertical separation (stagger)

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:825-959](), [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:241-319]()

### Parameter Calculation Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Trajectory Frame"] --> SetupBase["Setup Base Coordinates"]
    SetupBase --> FitRef["Fit Reference Frames"]
    FitRef --> BasePair{"Determine\nBase Pairing"}
    
    subgraph "Parameter Calculations"
        BasePair --> |"For each pair"| BPParams["Calculate Base Pair Parameters"]
        BPParams --> |"For consecutive pairs"| StepParams["Calculate Step Parameters"]
        StepParams --> HelicalParams["Calculate Helical Parameters"]
        BasePair --> |"For consecutive bases\nin strand"| SSParams["Calculate Single Strand Parameters"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Options"
        BPParams --> OutputBP["BP.<suffix>"]
        StepParams --> OutputStep["BPstep.<suffix>"]
        HelicalParams --> OutputHelix["Helix.<suffix>"]
        SSParams --> OutputSS["SS.<suffix>"]
        BPParams --> DataSets["DataSets"]
    end
    
    style BasePair fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:159-169](), [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:505-581]()

## Calculated Parameters

### Base Pair Parameters

These parameters describe the relative position and orientation of two bases in a pair:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Shear     | Displacement along x-axis |
| Stretch   | Displacement along y-axis |
| Stagger   | Displacement along z-axis |
| Buckle    | Rotation around x-axis |
| Propeller | Rotation around y-axis |
| Opening   | Rotation around z-axis |

### Base Pair Step Parameters

These describe the relative position and orientation of two consecutive base pairs:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Shift     | Displacement along x-axis |
| Slide     | Displacement along y-axis |
| Rise      | Displacement along z-axis |
| Tilt      | Rotation around x-axis |
| Roll      | Rotation around y-axis |
| Twist     | Rotation around z-axis |

### Helical Parameters

These describe the helical structure:

| Parameter      | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| X-displacement | Displacement of base pair from helical axis along x |
| Y-displacement | Displacement of base pair from helical axis along y |
| Helical rise   | Rise along helical axis |
| Inclination    | Inclination of base pair to helical axis |
| Tip            | Tip of base pair with respect to helical axis |
| Helical twist  | Twist around helical axis |

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.h:70-80](), [src/Action_NAstruct.h:96-110]()

## Using the NAstruct Command

### Basic Syntax

```
nastruct [<dataset name>] [resrange <range>] [sscalc] [naout <suffix>]
         [noheader] [resmap <ResName>:{A,C,G,T,U} ...] [calcnohb]
         [noframespaces] [baseref <file>] ...
         [bpmode {3dna|babcock}] [allhb]
         [hbcut <hbcut>] [origincut <origincut>] [altona | cremer]
         [zcut <zcut>] [zanglecut <zanglecut>] [groovecalc {simple | 3dna}]
         [axesout <file> [axesoutarg <arg> ...] [axesparmout <file>]]
         [bpaxesout <file> [bpaxesoutarg <arg> ...] [bpaxesparmout <file>]]
         [stepaxesout <file> [stepaxesoutarg <arg> ...] [stepaxesparmout <file>]]
         [{ refindex <#> | reference | ref <name> | first | allframes |
            specifiedbp pairs <b1>-<b2>,... }]
```

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:123-147]()

### Key Command Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `resrange <range>` | Residue range to analyze |
| `sscalc` | Calculate single strand parameters |
| `naout <suffix>` | Output file suffix |
| `baseref <file>` | Custom reference base file |
| `bpmode {3dna\|babcock}` | Base pair convention to use |
| `allhb` | Count all hydrogen bonds (not just Watson-Crick) |
| `altona \| cremer` | Sugar pucker calculation method |
| `groovecalc {simple\|3dna}` | Groove width calculation method |
| `axesout`, `bpaxesout`, `stepaxesout` | Write pseudo-trajectories with reference axes |
| `specifiedbp pairs <b1>-<b2>,...` | Explicitly specify base pairs |

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:190-249]()

### Command Examples

Basic usage:
```
nastruct naout dna.dat
```

Specific base pairs with custom output:
```
nastruct naout custom.dat specifiedbp pairs 1-16,2-15,3-14,4-13
```

With reference frame output:
```
nastruct naout analysis.dat axesout axes.pdb
```

Using different groove calculation:
```
nastruct naout groove.dat groovecalc 3dna
```

Sources: [test/Test_NAstruct/RunTest.sh:16-80]()

## Visualization of Reference Frames

The NAstruct command can generate pseudo-trajectories representing the reference frames of bases, base pairs, and base pair steps. These can be visualized with molecular visualization software.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Pseudo-Trajectory Output"
        BaseAxes["Base Axes (axesout)"]
        BPAxes["Base Pair Axes (bpaxesout)"]
        StepAxes["Step Axes (stepaxesout)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Atom Representation"
        Origin["Origin Atom (Orig)"]
        XAxis["X-Axis Atom (X)"]
        YAxis["Y-Axis Atom (Y)"]
        ZAxis["Z-Axis Atom (Z)"]
    end
    
    BaseAxes --> Origin
    BaseAxes --> XAxis
    BaseAxes --> YAxis
    BaseAxes --> ZAxis
    
    BPAxes --> Origin
    BPAxes --> XAxis
    BPAxes --> YAxis
    BPAxes --> ZAxis
    
    StepAxes --> Origin
    StepAxes --> XAxis
    StepAxes --> YAxis
    StepAxes --> ZAxis
```

In the pseudo-trajectory files, each reference frame is represented by four atoms:
- Origin atom: Represents the origin of the reference frame
- X-axis atom: Positioned one unit from origin along the x-axis
- Y-axis atom: Positioned one unit from origin along the y-axis
- Z-axis atom: Positioned one unit from origin along the z-axis

These representations can be used to visualize how the reference frames change during a trajectory, providing insight into structural dynamics.

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:82-120](), [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:492-503]()

## Implementation Details

### Reference Handling

CPPTRAJ includes built-in reference coordinates for standard nucleic acid bases:
- Adenine (A)
- Cytosine (C)
- Guanine (G)
- Thymine (T)
- Uracil (U)

These references define the standard orientation and positioning of each base and are used to establish reference frames.

Custom reference bases can be loaded using the `baseref` option, allowing for analysis of modified nucleotides.

Sources: [src/AxisType.cpp:32-111](), [src/AxisType.cpp:204-310]()

### Base Pair Detection

Base pairs are detected using several geometric criteria:

1. **Distance between origins**: The origins of the two reference frames must be within a specified cutoff distance (default: 5.0 Å)
2. **Z-axis angle**: The angle between the z-axes of the two bases must indicate proper orientation
3. **Vertical separation**: The vertical (z-axis) separation of the bases must be within a cutoff (default: 2.0 Å)
4. **Hydrogen bonds**: The presence of hydrogen bonds between donor and acceptor atoms

For Watson-Crick base pairs, specific hydrogen bond patterns are recognized:
- A-T/A-U: N6(A)-O4(T/U) and N1(A)-N3(T/U)
- G-C: O6(G)-N4(C), N1(G)-N3(C), and N2(G)-O2(C)

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:584-657](), [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:825-959]()

## Output Files

The NAstruct command can generate several output files:

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| BP.\<suffix\> | Base pair parameters (shear, stretch, stagger, buckle, propeller, opening) |
| BPstep.\<suffix\> | Base pair step parameters (shift, slide, rise, tilt, roll, twist, etc.) |
| Helix.\<suffix\> | Helical parameters (x-disp, y-disp, h-rise, inclination, tip, h-twist) |
| SS.\<suffix\> | Single strand parameters (DX, DY, DZ, RX, RY, RZ) |

These files are formatted as space-delimited text files with headers describing each column.

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:170-180](), [test/Test_NAstruct/RunTest.sh:16-80]()

## References

The NAstruct implementation is based on methods from the following publications:

1. Babcock MS, Pednault EPD, Olson WK (1994). "Nucleic Acid Structure Analysis: Mathematics for Local Cartesian and Helical Structure Parameters That Are Truly Comparable Between Structures", J. Mol. Biol. 237, 125-156.

2. Olson WK, et al. (2001). "A Standard Reference Frame for the Description of Nucleic Acid Base-pair Geometry", J. Mol. Biol. 313, 229-237.

3. El Hassan MA, Calladine CR (1998). "Two Distinct Modes of Protein-induced Bending in DNA", J. Mol. Biol. 282, 331-343. (Used for 3DNA groove calculations)

4. Lu XJ, Olson WK (2003). "3DNA: a software package for the analysis, rebuilding and visualization of three-dimensional nucleic acid structures", Nucleic Acids Res. 31(17), 5108-21.

Sources: [src/Action_NAstruct.h:12-31](), [src/Action_NAstruct.cpp:454-466]()

# Grid Inhomogeneous Solvation Theory (GIST)
